docs.title: Jefferies initiates coverage on NSE with ‘Buy’; here’s why it sees fresh growth potential
docs.text:
The National Stock Exchange (NSE) combines market leadership, structural growth, diversification and a natural hedge against volatility, said Jefferies as it initiated coverage on the stock exchange's shares with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of Rs 2,085 apiece, implying more than 17% upside potential.
 The international brokerage called NSE a “market leader with new growth optionality”, expecting the company to deliver a 15% revenue CAGR over FY27-29, despite past regulatory headwinds. India has seen an approximately 4x increase in direct equity investors since the COVID-19 pandemic, led by younger cohorts. Yet penetration is only 3% of the population, much lower when compared to 18% in China, Jefferies noted.
Besides structural tailwinds, exchanges offer a volatility hedge, as revenue is positively correlated with the VIX, given that options revenue is premium-based, unlike that of global peers, it explained.
 Also read | NSE shares hit record low as IPO lock-in expiry frees up stake worth Rs 3,247 cr for trading. How has the stock performed since listing? 
 NSE’s dependence on options is overstated: Jefferies
NSE is the market leader in cash equities, index F&O, stock F&O, and clearing & settlement. While around 60% of operating revenues come from equity options, weekly index options, which have faced regulatory action, account for.40% operating revenues, while the same for BSE stands at around 65%.
 Live Events
Low-turnover clients account for only 2-3%, limiting the risk from SEBI action to protect small traders, the international brokerage said, adding that it sees the equity options share in transaction revenues to fall to 50% from the current 60% over the next 5 years.
 NSE’s revenue to accelerate over FY28-29, says Jefferies
NSE’s operating revenue CAGR was 6% between FY24-26, as its equity F&O business was adversely impacted by regulatory changes and higher taxes. “We think these are now largely in the base. Hence, expect growth to improve to 15% over FY27-29 driven by equity options market share stabilizing at 65%, cash equity turnover growing at 16% led by IPOs, promoter/PE sell-downs, and tech infra revenues growing at 23% CAGR,” Jefferies said.
It added that NSE’s tech infra revenues, 8% of FY26 operating revenues and at lower AI risk, could rise to 11% by FY29 as the company adds more colocation racks. Commodity F&O, the new mutual fund ordering platform and EGRs (Electronic Gold Receipts) could add another 15% to revenue and PAT by FY30, which is not part of the brokerage’s base case. NSE is also exploring opportunities in corporate bond futures, GIFT City and Market Lens, it noted.
 NSE earnings expectations
Jefferies expects NSE’s EBITDA margin to expand by 200 bps to 78% by FY29 due to benefits from investments made in employees and technology over the last 3 years, revenue growth improving over FY27-29, and scale-up of new businesses.
The international brokerage’s target price implies 15% premium to its fair value for BSE, considering greater diversification, higher optionality, higher dividend yield, and structurally higher margins.
 Also read | Jio effect! Reliance beats Tata to become India's most valued conglomerate 
 NSE share price
 NSE shares made their much-awaited market debut on September 24, listing at Rs 1,800 apiece on BSE. This marked a premium of less than 1% over the IPO price of Rs 1,785. Within an hour of the muted debut, the shares jumped over 5% from the IPO price to hit a high of Rs 1,878, pushing the market capitalisation as high as Rs 4.64 lakh crore, before the stock began to decline.
Shares of NSE dropped to Rs 1,640.25 apiece earlier this month, their lowest level since listing. However, the stock has now recovered some losses to trade at Rs 1,791 apiece, higher than its IPO price.

docs.title: HUL shares rise 3% after Q2 results. Jefferies, Nomura cut target price but forecast 29% upside potential
docs.text:
Shares of FMCG bellwether Hindustan Unilever rose as much as 3% to their day’s high of Rs 1,864 on the BSE on Thursday, reporting a net profit of Rs 2,790 crore for the second quarter of FY27, marking a 4% increase from Rs 2,685 crore reported in the same quarter last year.
 The company’s revenue from operations came in at Rs 18,226 crore, up 15% from Rs 15,919 crore posted in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.
The company expects performance to improve in FY27 compared with FY26, driven by portfolio and channel transformation. However, commodity inflation is likely to persist in the near term, with the company guiding for its consolidated EBITDA margin to remain within the current range of 22-24%.
 Should you buy HUL shares?
Jefferies has retained a Buy call but with a reduced target price of Rs 2,350 (29% upside). The brokerage said calibrated price hikes and cost efficiencies will help protect margins. Jefferies expects the impact of inflation to persist in the short term, while HUL's portfolio, largely comprising daily essentials, remains relatively less elastic to price changes. Both urban and rural markets continue to report broad-based growth, with volume-led growth remaining a key priority for the company. HUL has also retained its medium-term margin guidance of 22-24%.
“We expect HUL to see volume-led growth, aided by improved, favourable government policies and a low base. This should percolate into a better margin trajectory in the medium term, as operating leverage benefits start to play out,” the brokerage said in a note.
 Live Events
Nomura has cut its target price for HUL to Rs 2,100 from Rs 2,450, implying an upside of 16%. Volume growth improved sequentially to 7% y-y in Q2, compared with Nomura’s estimate of 5%, despite an 8% y-y price hike. While this appears commendable, it comes against a flat base, translating into a two-year CAGR of 3.5% y-y, which Nomura believes is a more sustainable growth range than the headline volume growth.
The sharp price hike, coupled with a weak monsoon and droughts across several states, could affect the rabi crop and rural demand in the coming quarter, putting further pressure on volume growth. However, HUL highlighted that rural growth improved q-q in Q2 and that the categories it operates in have become more inelastic than in the past and compared with other discretionary categories. Sales growth of 15% y-y exceeded Nomura’s and consensus estimates of 11% and 10%, respectively, although the two-year CAGR stood at 7% y-y.
Domestic brokerage JM Financial also cut the target price by 4% to Rs 2,225 (22.5% upside). “We believe inflationary scenario augurs well for HUL as it accelerates share gains from unorganised/regional players, not to mention adequate levers to navigate the current volatile environment,” analysts said.
The stock has corrected 14% in the past three months and valuation is below the ten-year average. “We like HUL’s execution under the new CEO, but given the broader sector de-rating, we are cutting the target P/E to 40x (from 45x), yielding a revised TP of INR 2,225 (earlier INR 2,315).”
Priya Nair, CEO and Managing Director said the Indian economy remains resilient, with healthy macro indicators supporting a positive consumption environment. “We continue to invest in building long-term capabilities and remain anchored to the ‘Winning in New India’ strategy of delivering competitive, volume-led profit growth.”

docs.title: Bulls return as Fed rate pause, dip in US yields lift sentiment
docs.text:
Mumbai: Indian equities staged a broad-based recovery Thursday, with the Sensex rising 905 points and the Nifty closing above 22,900, as supportive global cues after the US Federal Reserve 's overnight decision to hold policy rates triggered buying across sectors.
 The US Federal Reserve voted to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged in a target range of 3.75% to 4%, triggering a retreat in US yields. The near-1% slide in US benchmark 10-year yields offered some relief to equities, although uncertainty over the global interest-rate outlook continued to weigh on investor sentiment. The 30-share BSE Sensex gained 905.01 points, or 1.24%, to settle at 74,151.04, while the NSE Nifty advanced 237.90 points, or 1.05%, to close at 22,936.75.
The rebound followed the previous session's weakness and was supported by buying in banking, financial services and other heavyweight stocks.
All sectoral indices except auto ended higher. Nifty Bank, Media, Infrastructure, PSU Bank, Private Bank and Energy indices gained around 1% each, while IT, Consumer Durables, Metal, Oil & Gas and Realty rose more than 0.5%.
 Read more: Trent Q2 Results: Cons profit jumps 25% YoY to Rs 468 crore; revenue climbs 22% 
 Live Events
Broader markets also inched up along with benchmark indices. The Nifty Midcap 150 index went up 0.8%, while Nifty Smallcap 250 index gained 0.6%.
"Domestic equities staged a strong recovery, reversing part of the weakness seen in the previous session," said Sunny Agrawal, head, fundamental research, SBI Securities. He said buying in large-cap stocks and strength in rate-sensitive sectors, including banking, financial services, FMCG and realty, contributed to the gains.
 Read more: Market Trading Guide: Eternal among 2 stocks to buy for Friday for healthy returns 
 Oil Risks 
However, crude oil prices above $110 a barrel remain a key macroeconomic risk for import-dependent economies such as India.
Brent crude remained elevated around $114-115 a barrel amid concerns over potential supply disruptions in West Asia.
Market direction will continue to depend on crude oil prices, geopolitical developments, foreign fund flows and movements in global bond yields, said Ajit Mishra, SVP Research Religare Broking.
He also said while the rebound improved near-term sentiment, sustained buying will be needed to confirm a durable recovery.
Foreign portfolio investors net sold shares worth ₹943 crore on Thursday taking the total net sales in October so far to ₹48,760 crore. Domestic institutions (DIIs) were net buyers to the tune of ₹1,924 crore, taking the cumulative net investments in equities to ₹63,037 crore in October so far.
On the technical front, Mishra said the Nifty's move above the 20-day exponential moving average (EMA) zone around 22,825 offered near-term relief and improved the prospects of an advance towards 23,100-23,300.
"The 22,500-22,700 zone is likely to provide immediate support, while 22,200-22,400 remains an important downside reference," he said.

docs.title: Indian jewellers wait for cheaper gold before festive buying spree
docs.text:
India’s gold market is entering its most important buying window with an unusual sense of restraint. Rather than rushing to build inventory before Diwali , many jewellers are waiting on the sidelines, convinced that the recent pullback in bullion still has room to deepen, NDTV Profit reported, citing MMTC-PAMP India Pvt. chief executive officer and managing director Samit Guha . 
 Festive demand meets a cautious trade 
The hesitation is most visible among larger jewellery chains, which typically account for a substantial share of organised sales. According to Guha, these retailers have not yet fully re-entered the market even after the latest decline in gold prices . By contrast, smaller and mid-sized jewellers have been the more active buyers, with some placing repeat orders as they replenish stocks in smaller quantities. 
 The pattern marks a shift from the usual playbook. When prices are rising, bigger players often accelerate purchases to secure supply before costs climb further. When they expect prices to soften, they trim inventories and delay fresh orders. That cautious stance appears to be guiding buying decisions now, as jewellers assess whether the correction in global bullion has further to run. 
 Price correction has changed the mood 
Gold slipped below $4,000 an ounce last week for the first time since July, extending a decline of about 24 per cent from the levels seen after the US-Iran war began in late February, according to the report. The metal had earlier surged to a record above $5,400 in January, highlighting how sharply sentiment has swung this year. 
 For Indian buyers, the move should normally have triggered stronger restocking. Instead, the market has remained subdued, reflecting both the expectation of lower prices and the strain created by policy changes. The report said demand has stayed weak through the year after the government more than doubled import duty to 15 per cent in May, raising landed costs for official imports . 
 Prime Minister Narendra Modi has repeatedly urged Indians to moderate gold purchases in order to help contain the widening trade deficit. Since the country imports almost all the gold it consumes, any rise in buying quickly feeds into the external account. The higher duty has also encouraged more informal trade, with some purchases shifting into cash-based transactions outside the formal market. 
 Why the market is behaving differently from China 
The caution in India stands in contrast to China, the world’s largest gold consumer, where household buying has reportedly picked up as prices have eased. That divergence matters because India is now moving into its strongest gold-buying season, when purchases usually cluster between October and December around Diwali . This year, the festival falls on November 8, making the next few weeks critical for jewellers, refiners and importers alike. 
The subdued start to the season has prompted fresh concerns about import volumes. Citi Research expects tighter import rules and weaker rural demand, hurt by El Nino-linked monsoon disruptions, to weigh on shipments. The brokerage estimates gold imports at about 106 tonnes in the October to December quarter, nearly half the historical fourth-quarter average of 212 tonnes. 
 Sales remain below last year’s pace 
At MMTC-PAMP , sales are still trailing last year’s levels, with demand skewed towards smaller coins and bars rather than larger jewellery-linked purchases, Guha said. September sales were roughly unchanged from a year earlier, while October has shown a modest pickup. Even so, the recovery remains tentative rather than broad-based. 
The company’s reading of the market suggests that jewellers are not rejecting gold outright. They are simply waiting for a better entry point. If prices stabilise or rebound, buying could return quickly, especially from larger chains that need to secure festive stock. As Guha put it, if gold turns higher again, purchases will follow. 
 For now, India’s jewellers appear to be betting that patience will pay. In a market shaped by volatile prices, higher duties and hesitant consumers, the biggest festive buying season may begin with caution rather than celebration.

docs.title: Noel, Chandra secret truce talks reach no conclusion
docs.text:
Mumbai: Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran and Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata held a secret meeting on Sunday that was arranged by former group veteran NA Soonawala in a move aimed at resolving the differences that have roiled the leadership of one of India's biggest conglomerates but it ended inconclusively, according to people with knowledge of the matter. Central to their talks were the holding company's listing, a proposed buyout of the Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group's stake in Tata Sons and Chandrasekaran's tenure as chairman, they said.
 Although the October 25 meeting is said to have ended with a mutual agreement over follow-up dialogue, the next day Noel Tata issued a letter challenging the decisions taken at the Tata Sons board meeting of September 17. He questioned the procedures and voting requirements that led to the approval of Chandrasekaran's reappointment, as well as potential conflicts of interest. He sought recordings of the board meeting and the final minutes and voting records in the October 26 letter, as ET reported previously.
The Sunday meeting is understood to have followed interventions by former Tata executives and some insiders amid concerns over implications of the rift for the group's brand, according to the people who spoke to ET on condition of anonymity. This was the first such meeting between the two sides since the September 17 board meeting, which approved another term for Chandra and backed Tata Sons listing. 
Noel Tata had opposed both moves.
Chandrasekharan and Noel Tata did not respond to queries from ET.
 Live Events
Executives close to the matter said former group veterans such as S Ramadorai, Ishaat Hussain and R Gopalakrishnan as well as insiders like Aloo Tata, Noel Tata's wife, and Geetanjali Kirloskar, chairperson and MD of Kirloskar Systems, had encouraged the meeting between the two sides. This could not be independently verified. Aloo Tata is the sister of Shapoor Mistry, chairman of the SP Group. Noel Tata's son Neville is married to Manasi, Geetanjali Kirloskar's daughter.
The meeting was held at Noel Tata's residence in south Mumbai, said the people cited. Chandrasekaran raised concerns about the lack of communication between the two sides and the need to sort out disagreements amicably, they said.
Noel Tata reiterated that Tata Sons should remain privately held and that the SP Group should be offered Rs 25,000 crore through partial monetisation of its 18.4% stake. Chandrasekaran is said to have responded that Tata Sons would consider it and that a listing would complicate the matter. Chandrasekaran is understood to have said the listing decision was not within his control and was mandated by regulatory requirements imposed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
The SP Group, led by Shapoor Mistry, has backed a listing as a way to improve transparency and monetise its investment. The Tata Trusts, which hold a majority stake in Tata Sons, oppose the listing and have said alternatives should be considered.
The RBI had rejected Tata Sons' proposal to surrender its registration as an upper-layer non-banking financial company. That meant it was subject to rules requiring such entities to list within three years of classification.
Noel Tata is also understood to have raised the matter of Chandrasekaran's reappointment and that he should retire at 65, in line with the group's policy. Chandrasekaran indicated he would abide by the policy but said he needed to complete the major projects that are underway such as those at Tata Electronics, Air India and Tata Digital, the people said. Noel Tata is understood to have said that he could take the reappointment issue to court if it remained unresolved.
People aware of the discussions said that the chairman of Tata Sons was keen to pursue an amicable resolution of the rift and not prolonging the impasse.
"The big picture was that the Tata Group is bigger than individuals and must be protected," said one of the persons who spoke to ET.
Noel Tata, however, is keen that the key concerns raised by him should be addressed by Tata Sons. "Tata is determined that the issues raised are valid and cannot be sidelined," said the person cited.
The Tata Sons board had reappointed Chandrasekaran for a second five-year term beginning February 2027, with Noel Tata casting the sole dissenting vote. Chandrasekaran's current term ends on February 20, 2027.
Noel Tata has also raised with the Tata Sons board the issue of investments exceeding Rs 100 crore in group subsidiaries requiring his approval, the people said. This could raise questions about the respective powers of the Tata Sons board and those of the Tata Trusts, which collectively owns about 66% of the holding company.
Legal experts said dialogue remained a way to resolve the dispute, while noting that legal action could be initiated if there were violations of the law.
"The best course of action is to settle the matters through mutual discussion and conciliation," said Ashish K Singh, managing partner at Capstone Legal. "Even courts encourage out-of-court settlement of disputes in matters which involve multiple stakeholders and are in tune with principles of corporate governance."
Multiple notices won't be needed before initiating legal action, said a senior lawyer. "If there is an infraction of law, the court can be approached directly without any delay," he said.

docs.title: Vande Bharat, Visakha Express & 7 more trains cancelled, 14 diverted after Cyclone Arnab triggers flood sc
docs.text:
Cyclone Arnab has disrupted train operations on the Howrah-Chennai route, with nine trains cancelled and 14 diverted on Thursday after the Bahuda river crossed the danger mark near two railway bridges in Odisha's Ganjam district. The East Coast Railway said services were affected in the Ichchapuram-Jhadupudi section of the Visakhapatnam Division after water levels rose above the danger mark at two bridges. Train operations will resume once water levels recede and the affected section is declared safe.
 Among the services cancelled were the Vande Bharat Express between Bhubaneswar and Visakhapatnam, the Bhubaneswar-Visakhapatnam Intercity Express and the Visakha Express , which connects Bhubaneswar with Secunderabad in Telangana.
 Read more - Nitin Gadkari says no challan for speeding up to 20% over the limit: What he told officials, when challans should be issued & what motorists must know 
 Cyclone Arnab: Why have train services been disrupted in Odisha?
Heavy rainfall associated with Cyclone Arnab has caused the Bahuda river to swell, affecting railway infrastructure in Ganjam district. According to the East Coast Railway, the district received 550 mm of rainfall, leading to a sharp rise in the river's water level. The water level at Baghalati Dam on the Bahuda river also crossed the danger mark following the downpour.
 Read more - Closed on Diwali: 15+ railway reservation centres in Delhi to remain shut or operate for limited hours on November 8; check full list before visiting 
 Live Events
As a result, water levels rose above the danger mark at railway bridges along the Ichchapuram-Jhadupudi section, prompting authorities to restrict train movements as a precautionary measure.
The disruption has affected services operating along the busy Howrah-Chennai route, with railway officials monitoring conditions before allowing normal operations to resume.
 Which trains have been cancelled and diverted?
The East Coast Railway confirmed that nine trains had been cancelled and 14 others diverted to ensure passenger safety.
The major cancelled services include:
 Vande Bharat Express between Bhubaneswar and Visakhapatnam
 Bhubaneswar-Visakhapatnam Intercity Express
 Visakha Express between Bhubaneswar and Secunderabad
 Several other trains operating on the affected route have also been diverted. Passengers are advised to check the latest updates from the railway authorities before travelling, as services remain subject to changes depending on weather and track conditions.
An East Coast Railway official said, "Nine trains have been cancelled, and 14 others diverted to ensure passenger safety. Railway officials are closely monitoring the situation. Train services will be restored once the water level recedes and the section is declared safe for train operations."
 Railways arrange food and water for stranded passengers
The disruption has left passengers stranded at different locations, prompting the railways to arrange essential assistance.
The East Coast Railway said food and drinking water were being provided to affected passengers. Additional staff have also been deployed to guide travellers, address their grievances and provide necessary assistance.
Railway officials are continuing to monitor water levels around the affected bridges. Normal train operations will resume only after the water recedes and the section is considered safe for train movement.

docs.title: Anita Advani-Rajesh Khanna relationship: SC rejects plea; Actor claimed Dimple, Twinkle and Akshay evicted
docs.text:
The Supreme Court on Thursday refused to entertain former actor Anita Advani ’s plea seeking legal recognition of her alleged relationship with late Bollywood superstar Rajesh Khanna as a marriage. The bench described the case as “luxury litigation” while dismissing her challenge to a Bombay High Court order. A bench comprising Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale said it found no reason to interfere with the high court’s April 1 order.
 Advani’s lawyer told the court that the case was about securing dignity for her client. The counsel argued that the civil suit seeking a declaration of her relationship with Khanna was rooted in her desire for recognition. However, the bench was not persuaded by the argument and declined to entertain the petition.
 How the legal battle between Anita Advani and Rajesh Khanna’s family began
Advani claimed that she had been in a live-in relationship with Khanna for several years before she was asked to leave his Mumbai bungalow, Aashirwad, in 2012. The eviction allegedly took place after Khanna’s estranged wife, veteran actor Dimple Kapadia, along with their daughter Twinkle Khanna and son-in-law Akshay Kumar , intervened. Khanna died in July 2012. 
Following his death, Advani approached the courts seeking legal recognition of her alleged relationship with the superstar. Her civil suit was rejected by a Mumbai sessions court in 2017, prompting her to challenge the decision. The Bombay High Court subsequently dismissed her appeal, leading her to approach the Supreme Court.
 Anita Advani’s domestic violence complaint
The legal dispute also involved proceedings under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. In 2013, Advani filed a complaint before a magistrate against Kapadia, her daughters and Akshay Kumar. She sought monthly maintenance and a three-bedroom apartment in Mumbai’s upscale Bandra area.
 Live Events
Kapadia and her family challenged the complaint, seeking the dismissal of the proceedings. In 2015, the Bombay High Court quashed the complaint, holding that Advani’s relationship with Khanna did not qualify as a relationship in the nature of marriage under the domestic violence law. The court also observed that Khanna’s family members could not be drawn into the proceedings when Advani had never lived with them.
 Who is Anita Advani?
Anita Advani is a former actor who appeared in a handful of films, including Saazish and Daasi . She came into the spotlight over her claim that she had shared a long-term domestic relationship with Rajesh Khanna, one of Hindi cinema’s most celebrated stars. Khanna, widely regarded as Bollywood’s first superstar, died in July 2012. His personal life and relationship with Kapadia had attracted public attention for years.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

Reliance Power 's board of directors on Monday approved the issuance of up to 46.20 crore equity shares/warrants worth Rs 1,525 crore via preferential allotment mode.
 The board has set the issue price at Rs 33 per share.
The issue price of equity shares/warrants is at a discount of 13% over Monday's closing price of Rs 38.15 on the NSE. The announcement was made after market hours and Reliance Power shares on Monday ended with gains of Rs 1.81 or 4.98% over the previous closing price.
 Reliance Infrastructure Limited, the promoter of the company, will enhance its equity stake by over Rs 600 crore, a company filing said. The other investors in the preferential issue are Authum Investment and Infrastructure Limited and Sanatan Financial Advisory Services Private Limited.
The proceeds from the preferential issue will be utilised to expand business operations directly and/or through investment in subsidiaries and joint ventures, debt reduction and for general corporate purposes, the filing said.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.
 WATCH LIVE TODAY: Press conference with #FOMC Chair Powell at 2:30 p.m. ET: https://t.co/1uJrua5qsH https://t.co/FJa6TbkDMt pic.twitter.com/87g5NJITsz 
— Federal Reserve (@federalreserve) September 18, 2024 
By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

Nomura has maintained its 'Buy' rating on SBI Life Insurance, retaining the stock as its top pick in the life insurance sector, despite cutting its target price to Rs 2,340 from Rs 2,440 after raising its risk-free rate assumption.
The brokerage said SBI Life's value of new business (VNB) margin stood at 29.2% in Q2FY27, beating its estimate by 50 basis points. Excluding the impact of GST, VNB margins in the September quarter and first half of FY27 would have been 30% and 28.8%, respectively.
Total annualised premium equivalent (APE) grew 7.4% year-on-year in Q2FY27, led by non-participating products, which rose 27%, annuity products, up 28%, and individual protection, up 14%. Nomura said the scale-up in high-margin products was a key driver of the expansion in VNB margins.
 SBI Life Insurance 's individual APE growth stood at 12% year-on-year in the first half of FY27, below its full-year guidance of 14-15%. However, management reaffirmed its growth guidance, with the third quarter typically a strong period for the insurer, driven by the bancassurance channel.
Nomura expects APE to grow 16% and VNB to rise 17% year-on-year in FY27. It believes sustained momentum in non-par products, annuity and individual protection could support VNB margins of 26-29% in Q3 and Q4FY27, translating into a 27.6% margin for the full year.
Non-par and annuity products offer support
Nomura expects non-par guaranteed products to see stronger demand over the next couple of quarters amid a sharp rise in benchmark yields.
SBI Life's management indicated that it had already increased guarantee rates and that the pickup in these products through the agency channel had been encouraging. The company is also set to launch a new annuity product.
SBI Life's stock has declined 20% year-to-date, compared with a 13% fall in the Nifty, largely due to concerns over distribution reforms. According to management, SBI Life is the least impacted by the regulator's consultation paper.
Nomura rolled forward its valuation to September 2027 and raised its risk-free rate assumption to 7.25% from 6.25%, taking its cost of funds to 13.9%. This led to a reduction in the target price to Rs 2,340, implying 1.9 times September 2028 embedded value.
The brokerage cited a return on embedded value of 18.8% as of September 2026 and its 17% VNB growth estimate as reasons to remain positive on the stock. SBI Life currently trades at 1.5 times one-year forward price-to-embedded-value.
Nomura flagged the risk that lower commission structures under distribution reforms could intensify competition in SBI Life's home market, particularly from large urban-focused players.

Nomura has maintained its 'Buy' rating on Max Financial Services but cut its target price to Rs 2,000 from Rs 2,080 after raising its risk-free rate assumption, even as Axis Max Life Insurance delivered a stronger-than-expected improvement in value of new business (VNB) margins.
Axis Max Life, in which Max Financial Services holds an 80.01% stake, reported VNB margins of 27% in Q2FY27 and 25.4% in the first half, beating Nomura's estimates by 130 basis points and 70 basis points, respectively.
Management attributed the margin expansion to a favourable product mix, with annuity business growing 119% year-on-year and group protection rising 20%, alongside a lower operating expense ratio and improved product-level profitability. The expense ratio declined 4 percentage points quarter-on-quarter and 1.9 percentage points year-on-year.
 Nomura raises FY27 VNB margin estimate to 26% 
Nomura expects annualised premium equivalent (APE) growth of 17-18% year-on-year in Q3 and Q4FY27, translating into 15% growth for FY27. It expects VNB to grow 19% year-on-year in FY27.
The brokerage expects momentum in annuity business to continue, supported by a new product launch planned for Q4FY27. The decline in non-participating savings products is expected to stabilise as the base becomes favourable from Q3FY27.
Nomura's quarterly estimates indicate VNB margins slightly above 26% over the next two quarters. It has raised its FY27 VNB margin estimate to 26%, implying 19% year-on-year growth in VNB.
 Distribution reforms remain a key monitorable 
Management has reported constructive discussions with the regulator on the proposed distribution reforms. It has sought transition periods, highlighted the importance of credit life products and made suggestions on a single cap, among other issues.
Axis Max Life remains confident of bringing down its expense of management ratio from the current 25% to 16-17.5%. Management has also suggested excluding GST from the EOM calculation as another potential lever.
Nomura said the insurer's core operating performance remains healthy, but negotiations around distribution reforms remain a key trigger for the stock. The brokerage noted that the proposed changes have weighed more heavily on pure retail life insurers such as Axis Max Life than on larger players with group portfolios.
Nomura rolled forward its valuation to September 2027 and raised its risk-free rate assumption to 7.25% from 6.25%, resulting in a reduction in its target price to Rs 2,000 from Rs 2,080.

Shares of Tata Capital settled over 5 percent on Thursday’s trading session, extending their gains after the non-banking financial company (NBFC) reported strong earnings in the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27.
With the health earnings report, brokerages have their positive outlook on the stock, citing healthy loan growth, improving operating leverage and stable asset quality, while identifying a recovery in net interest margins as a key trigger for further earnings improvement.
The Tata group stock opened at Rs 308.60 on the BSE and climbed 6.1 percent to hit the day’s high of Rs 328.50, compared with the last closing price of Rs 309.35. The stock eventually settled 5.54 per cent or Rs 17.15 higher at Rs 326.50.
The company announced its Q2 FY27 results on Tuesday, reporting strong growth in profitability and assets under management (AUM).
 Tata Capital reported a 51 percent year-on-year (YoY) growth in consolidated net profit to Rs 1,660 crore for the September quarter of FY27. The company had posted a net profit of Rs 1,097 crore in the July-September period of FY26.
Net total income rose 24 per cent to Rs 4,676 crore during the September quarter of FY27, from Rs 3,774 crore in the corresponding period a year ago.
The non-bank lender’s Assets Under Management (AUM) stood at Rs 3,08,030 crore, up 26 per cent year-on-year.
In a separate exchange filing, Tata Capital said its board approved a proposal for the enhancement of the existing medium-term note programme from USD 2 billion to USD 3 billion and, subject to market conditions, issuance of foreign currency bonds/debt instruments under the MTN Programme, in one or more tranches, by way of external commercial borrowings.
 Brokerages on Tata Capital: Check share price targets 
 JM Financial on Tata Capital share: Buy, target price Rs 400 
Brokerage firm JM Financial maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Tata Capital with a target price of Rs 400, citing good quarter with strong profit growth, healthy AUM expansion and improving operating leverage.
The brokerage said the company's profit after tax rose 64 percent YoY and 13 percent quarter-on-quarter, exceeding its estimates by 12 percent. Return on assets (RoA) and return on equity (RoE) improved to 2.4 percent and 14.8 percent, respectively.
However, the brokerage flagged that net interest margin (NIM) remained a key concern. Calculated NIM declined 9 basis points sequentially to around 4.9 percent, marking the fourth consecutive quarterly decline. The contraction was driven by a 13-basis-point increase in the calculated cost of funds, partly reflecting the impact of EBLR- and repo-linked bank borrowings.
Consequently, net interest income grew 23 per cent YoY and 4 per cent quarter-on-quarter, below the brokerage's estimates, despite AUM growth of 26 per cent YoY and 6 per cent sequentially.
“As a result, net interest income (NII) grew only 23%/4% YoY/QoQ (-2% JMFe) despite strong AUM growth of 26%/6% (32% YoY ex-Motor Finance). Higher other income (due to gain from the PE business) and lower opex offset the NII miss and weak core fees, so PPOP was slightly ahead of our estimates,” the brokerage said.
JM Financial noted that credit costs remained contained at 0.86 per cent, while management retained its existing guidance.
“The levers available are 20-25bps PLR hikes from November 2026, a largely floating loan book (66% versus 49% of borrowings) and a rising mix of high-yield retail,” it added.
JM Financial values Tata Capital at 2.8 times its estimated FY28 book value per share, based on average RoA of 2.2 per cent and RoE of 16 per cent over FY27-FY29.
 Systematix Institutional Equities on Tata Capital share: Buy, target price Rs 400 
Systematix Institutional Equities also maintained its ‘Buy’ outlook on Tata Capital, with a target price of Rs 400, valuing the stock at 2.7x estimated FY28 adjusted book value.
The brokerage said the company's Q2 FY27 profit of around Rs 1,830 crore was approximately 11 percent above its estimates and 13 percent ahead of Bloomberg consensus expectations. Improving operating leverage and lower-than-expected credit costs supported the performance.
The cost-to-income ratio improved by 100 basis points sequentially, while credit costs declined 10 basis points to 0.86 per cent.
AUM growth was led by the corporate and small and medium enterprise (SME) segments, which expanded 54 per cent and 34 per cent YoY, respectively. Retail AUM grew 17 per cent despi

 Nomura maintains Buy on Allied Blenders with Rs 850 target.
 Q2 sales rose 16% YoY, beating analyst estimates.
 Mass-premium volume growth offset weakness in premium brands.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
Nomura has maintained its 'Buy' rating on Allied Blenders & Distillers and retained its target price of Rs 850 after the liquor maker reported better-than-expected sales and operating profit for the second quarter of FY27, supported by a recovery in mass-premium volumes.
Consolidated sales rose 16% year-on-year to Rs 11.5 billion, ahead of Nomura's and consensus estimates of 10% and 8.6%, respectively. Volume growth of around 11% to 10 million cases was in line with the brokerage's forecast, while realisation per case increased 3.2%, compared with its estimate of 2.5%, driven by a better product and state mix.
Operating profit grew 11% year-on-year, beating Nomura's and consensus estimates of 7.5% and 8.7%, respectively, as higher sales offset pressure on margins. Profit after tax rose 11.2% year-on-year to Rs 700 million, compared with estimates of a 1.5% decline and profit of Rs 630 million, respectively.
 Mass-premium volumes offset weakness in premium brands 
Mass-premium sales, which accounted for 44% of revenue, grew 16% year-on-year, significantly above Nomura's estimate of 5%. Volumes rose around 16% to 5.5 million cases, the highest in 12 quarters, driven by brandy and whisky demand in southern states and exports.
The Prestige and Above (P&A) segment, which contributed 56% of sales, reported revenue growth of 13.5%. However, volume growth of 6% to 4.5 million cases fell short of Nomura's estimate of 10%.
ICONiQ White volumes grew 21% year-on-year and 4% sequentially to 3.2 million cases, below the brokerage's forecast of 30% growth. The P&A portfolio excluding ICONiQ White continued to decline 20% year-on-year, although it grew 3% sequentially.
Allied Blenders has expanded its premium whisky portfolio with the launch of The Indian Edit across Maharashtra, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Assam, Tripura, Rajasthan and Goa. The company has also relaunched Officer's Choice Blue with premium packaging in Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Haryana and West Bengal, with plans to enter more markets in phases.
 Margin pressure persists; FY28 operating margin guidance at 18% 
Gross profit margin stood at 45.3%, up 90 basis points year-on-year but down 64 basis points sequentially, below Nomura's estimate of 46%. The brokerage attributed the pressure to higher costs linked to the West Asia crisis and expects premiumisation and backward integration benefits to begin from the third quarter of FY27.
Operating profit margin declined 55 basis points year-on-year to 12.1%, below Nomura's and consensus estimates of 12.4% and 12.7%, respectively. The company increased brand investments behind its core offerings and newly launched luxury portfolio, with other costs rising 26% year-on-year.
The company expects operating profit margin to reach 18% in FY28, while its FY29 margin guidance has been raised from 19% to 19.5%.
Net debt-to-EBITDA and net debt-to-equity stood at 2.2 times and 0.8 times, marginally above the company's stated financial framework of 2 times and 0.75 times, respectively, due to milestone-based capital expenditure payments. Management expects both metrics to return within the stated framework by the end of FY27.
 Nomura maintains 'Buy', target price at Rs 850 
Nomura expects Allied Blenders to deliver earnings per share (EPS) compound annual growth of 26% over FY26-29. It values the company at 48 times September 2028 estimated EPS, at the lower end of the sector average, and expects new launches, growth in the Prestige and Above portfolio and backward integration to support mid-teen sales growth, mid-twenties EPS growth and a 370-basis-point expansion in EBITDA margin over FY26-29.
The brokerage maintained its 'Buy' rating and target price of Rs 850. It identified delays in execution and a slower shift towards premium products as key downside risks.

docs.title: Oil and gas stocks to buy: ONGC vs Oil India shares - Kotak Securities raises FY27 forecast to $100; know preferred pick
docs.text:
Dated Brent crude has averaged $126 per barrel so far in October and $104 per barrel to date in FY27, according to the brokerage. Although oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered significantly, renewed attacks on Saudi infrastructure and oil tankers have heightened concerns over potential supply disruptions. Crude and product tanker rates have also climbed to multi-year highs. The brokerage believes the policy environment for domestic upstream companies has improved following amendments to the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Act, royalty reforms and the government's Samudra Manthan initiative. It also highlighted the favourable pricing framework for gas from new wells, linked to 12% of Brent crude prices. ONGC remains the brokerage's preferred pick in the upstream oil and gas space, supported by a stronger medium-term production outlook, improving gas realisations and attractive valuations. Despite earlier setbacks at its KG-DWN-98/2 asset, ONGC's outlook is improving, with higher realisations from new-well gas and production growth from new fields expected to support performance. Its technical service partnership with BP for the Western Offshore asset, which accounts for around 70% of its production, is also expected to strengthen the medium-term outlook. In contrast, Oil India's limited reserves could constrain oil production after a near-term ramp-up, while weak oil and gas realisations have weighed on its overall margins. However, its gas production outlook remains relatively better, the brokerage noted. Kotak Institutional Equities has raised its FY27 earnings estimates for both companies by 16–17%, driven by higher crude oil and new-well gas realisations. Its FY28 and FY29 earnings-per-share estimates have been revised marginally higher due to increased other income, while volume assumptions remain unchanged. The brokerage has reiterated its Buy rating on ONGC and raised its fair value to ₹ 360 per share from ₹ 355 earlier. Against the 27 October closing price of ₹ 230, this implies an upside potential of around 57%. For Oil India, it has maintained its Sell rating and increased its fair value estimate to ₹ 365 from ₹ 360. Compared with the 27 October closing price of ₹ 457, the revised target implies a downside of around 20%. ONGC therefore remains the brokerage's preferred upstream stock, with its production outlook, improving realisations and valuation comfort underpinning the preference. docs.title: Top stocks to buy for long term: Pankaj Pandey of ICICI Securities suggests Crompton Greaves, Kotak Bank, 3 others
docs.text:
Top stocks to buy for long term: The Indian stock market has been under strong pressure this year due to heightened geopolitical tensions, elevated oil prices, and massive foreign capital outflow.The Nifty is down more than 12% this year so far; from its all-time high of 26,373, the index is down 14%.Pankaj Pandey, the head of research at ICICI Securities, underscored that markets are currently navigating a phase of heightened volatility, with the Nifty and broader market indices witnessing a meaningful correction from their recent highs.However, Pandey added that the weakness is less a reflection of any fundamental deterioration in the domestic earnings cycle and more a consequence of a confluence of external pressures - elevated crude prices, rising domestic and global bond yields, and heightened geopolitical uncertainty.Pandey pointed out that the underlying earnings picture remains encouraging."The listed universe, so far in the current earnings season, has delivered over 20%+ growth in both topline and PAT, providing increasing evidence that the domestic corporate earnings cycle is gaining traction. This resilience in earnings, despite a challenging macro backdrop, reinforces our core thesis of an earnings-led recovery in Indian equities," said Pandey.Pandey emphasised that the recent correction needs to be viewed in the context of price adjustment rather than a fundamental reset."With valuations having moderated meaningfully, the risk-reward equation is gradually becoming more favourable, particularly for quality businesses where earnings visibility remains intact," said Pandey.Pandey believes the next leg of the market may be driven less by liquidity or multiple expansion and increasingly by fundamental earnings delivery - a healthier and more sustainable foundation for returns."We see no material risks to our 16% CAGR Nifty earnings estimates over FY26-28E. We expect markets to deliver healthy double-digit returns over the next 12 months," said Pandey.Stock picks for long term
Pandey recommends buying the following five stocks for the next one year:
Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals | Previous close: ₹204 | Target price: ₹275 | Upside potential: 35%
Pandey said Crompton Greaves is a leading FMEG player, wherein nearly 76% of its revenue comes from electrical consumer durables (fans, pumps, appliances), nearly 13% from lighting, and the balance from Butterfly Gandhimathi.

Stocks to buy today | Jefferies India stock recommendations | Shares to buy today: The NSE shares have been reeling under the upper price band of ₹1,785 after hitting the record high of ₹1,878 per share on the listing date. NSE share price finished at ₹1777.05 per share on the BSE on Wednesday. However, Jefferies India is still bullish on NSE shares, provided there is a trend reversal on Dalal Street. The global investment bank has set the NSE share price target of ₹2,300 for long-term investors in the upside scenario. The Jefferies India report has also noted that, in the event of a downside trend, the NSE share may touch ₹1,600. In the base-case scenario, the NSE share price may touch ₹2,085 apiece, delivering around 17% returns to long-term investors.
NSE shares | Why is Jefferies bullish?
Calling NSE a hedge against volatility, the Jefferies India report said that India has seen a 4x increase in direct equity investors since COVID, led by younger cohorts. Yet penetration is only 3% of the population vs. 18% in China. Besides structural tailwinds, exchanges offer a volatility hedge, as revenue is positively correlated with the VIX, given that options revenue is premium-based, unlike that of global peers.
“NSE is the market leader in cash equities, index F&O, stock F&O, and clearing & settlement. While c.60% of operating revenues come from equity options, weekly index options, which have faced regulatory action, account for 40% opposit revenues (BSE: 65%). Low-turnover clients account for only 2-3%, limiting the risk from SEBI action to protect small traders. We see the equity options share in transaction revenues to fall to 50% from the current 60% over the next 5 years,” the Jefferies India report said.
Jefferies India expects fast revenue growth for NSE
Expecting fast growth in the NSE's revenue, Jefferies India said that the NSE's operating revenue CAGR was 6% between FY24-26, as its equity F&O business was adversely impacted by regulatory changes and higher taxes. We think these are now largely in the base. Hence, expect growth to improve to 15% over FY27-29e, driven by (1) equity options market share stabilising at 65%, (2) cash equity turnover growing at 16% led by IPOs, promoter/PE sell-downs, and (3) tech infra revenues growing at 23% CAGR.Pointing towards the new avenues for revenue for the NSE, Jefferies India said, "NSE's tech infra revenues, 8% of FY26 opposite revenues and at lower AI risk, could rise to 11% by FY29e as the company adds more colocation racks (JEFe: 600 racks in 2 years). Commodity F&O, the new mutual fund ordering platform and EGRs (Electronic Gold Receipts) could add another c.15% to revenue/PAT by FY30e, which are not part of our base case. NSE is also exploring opportunities in corporate bond futures, GIFT City and Market Lens."“We expect EBITDA margin to expand by 200bps to 78% by FY29e due to: (1) benefits from investments made in employees and technology over the last 3 years, (2) revenue growth improving over FY27-29e, and (3) scale-up of new businesses,” the global investment bank added.NSE shares | Top 4 reasons to buyListing out foour major reasons for the long-term investors to buy NSE shares, the Jefferies India report said, “NSE trades at 34x FY28e EPS, a 18% discount to BSE. We have a different view. Our PT of Rs2,085 is based on 35x Dec'28e EPS, 15% premium to our fair value for BSE, considering: (1) greater diversification, (2) higher optionality, (3) higher dividend yield, and (4) structurally higher margins.”However, the global investment bank maintained that, in the upside scenario, NSE shares may touch ₹2,300, whereas in the downside scenario, they may touch ₹1,600.Disclaimer: This story is for educational and informational purposes only.  Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India reported a 22.2% year-on-year rise in consolidated profit to ₹ 77 crore in the September quarter of calendar year 2026, compared with ₹ 63 crore in the corresponding period last year.
Revenue from operations increased 12.4% year-on-year to ₹ 263 crore from ₹ 234 crore. EBITDA rose to ₹ 102 crore from ₹ 85 crore, while the EBITDA margin improved to 38.7% from 36.4%. Meanwhile, total expenses climbed to ₹ 164.8 crore from ₹ 152.8 crore in the year-ago quarter.
The company reported 19% year-on-year growth in domestic sales. For the nine months ended September 2026, revenue from operations grew 16% to ₹ 728 crore from ₹ 627.4 crore in the corresponding period last year. Domestic sales increased 15%, supported by product relaunches, while exports recorded 19% growth.
Commenting on the performance, Himanshu Bakshi, managing director of Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India, said the September-quarter results reflected the effective execution of the company's strategy and the strength of its product portfolio.
He added that growth was supported by higher volumes and market share gains across key brands. Continued investments in brand building, expanding distribution networks and engaging with healthcare professionals were also helping the company strengthen its reach among consumers.
Sanofi share price has gained 5.40% over the past week, indicating a recent recovery after sustained selling pressure. However, the stock has declined 11.07% over the past month and 24.60% year-to-date.
On a one-year basis, Sanofi shares have fallen 26.38%, reflecting significant weakness in its overall performance despite the recent weekly gains.
Gaurav Garg, Head - Research, Lemonn, believes that Sanofi Consumer shares rallied sharply following the announcement, but the stock has been trading well below its earlier highs, and a single strong quarter is not enough to confirm a durable trend reversal.
Garg further recommended to avoid chasing the immediate post-results rally and wait for consolidation before considering fresh exposure and existing investors to continue to hold if their investment thesis remains intact, but should reassess the position if the stock fails to sustain its recovery.

Mint Money 
 Co-pay shifts the bill, doesn’t necessarily cut health care costs: Digit Insurance's Kamesh Goyal
 Deepti Bhaskaran 8 min read 29 Oct 2026, 12:51 PM IST 
 Summary
 Digit Insurance chairman Kamesh Goyal argues that co-payments alone cannot contain healthcare costs. Transparent hospital pricing, simpler insurance products and expense rules that reflect retail customers’ costs are also needed. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Rising healthcare costs, higher health insurance premiums and claims disputes are testing consumers’ trust in health insurance. As insurers point to opaque hospital pricing and propose that policyholders bear part of each claim through co-payments, customers risk being squeezed further.
 In this interview, Kamesh Goyal, chairman, Go Digit Group of Companies, discusses affordability, claims and distribution reform, and why transparent hospital pricing, simpler products and expense rules that reflect the cost of serving retail customers are key to delivering better value.
 Will a mandatory 10% co-pay help control rising health insurance costs?
 Co-pay itself is not new. Customers already have the choice in many products to take a co-pay and receive a lower premium. When I lived in Germany, I chose a 2,500 euro deductible because it reduced my premium. I could have chosen a lower deductible; the choice was mine.
 Based on media reports about the proposal, what concerns me is the reported idea of making co-pay compulsory even for existing customers at renewal. If somebody bought a policy without co-pay, paid a higher premium for that benefit, and has renewed it for years, is it fair to change that promise later? I do not think so.
 The bigger question is whether co-pay will actually control healthcare costs. Co-pay can reduce the insurer’s share of the claim and, if the benefit is passed on, the customer’s premium. But it changes who pays the bill; it does not necessarily reduce the overall cost of healthcare.
 How can hospital costs be controlled?
 We should first stop blaming one another. Insurers, healthcare providers and customers are all stakeholders. The insurance industry already has data on procedure costs, average length of stay, consultant charges and readmissions. Using standard diagnosis and procedure classifications, including ICD coding where appropriate, we should compare treatment costs across similar categories of hospitals.
 We could begin with the 10, 20 or 25 most common procedures and publish hospital-wise data for the past five years. Primary, secondary and tertiary hospitals should be compared within their categories. That would show how costs have changed and give us a factual basis for discussions with healthcare providers.
 For planned treatment, customers should be able to see the normal treatment pathway, expected length of stay, typical cost range and how the hospital they are considering compares with hospitals of a similar category. Hospitals need not all charge the same, because infrastructure and clinical capability differ, but unusually high costs should become visible and explainable. Insurers, hospitals, government agencies and regulators can then identify where the variation arises and what can reasonably be corrected.
 Also, we need to use healthcare infrastructure more appropriately. Not everything requires a tertiary-care hospital or a specialist. India needs stronger primary and secondary care, more generalist doctors, better triage and greater use of appropriate home healthcare, particularly for chronic conditions and elder care.
 How can simpler products and clearer claims improve transparency?
 After transparency in hospital costs, the next step is product simplification. The customer should know what is covered and what is not. The hospital should know what the insurer will pay, and the insurer’s claims process should become simpler because those boundaries are clear.
 Health products are increasingly differentiated through features and bells and whistles that customers find difficult to value. Some additions may sound attractive but do not materially improve protection, while making products harder to compare and allowing a higher premium to be charged.
 I would prefer a strong minimum base health product, with additional benefits available as separately priced riders. The customer should be able to see the price of the base protection and the price of every additional benefit. We do not need a large number of substantially similar products if the real differences can be expressed transparently through riders.
 We need standard product guidelines that are not complex, and hospital bills can also be standardized. There is no need for every hospital to use a different billing format. Room eligibility and the effect of choosing a different room should be clear. Without simplicity and transparency at these levels, the customer’s experience will not change enough.
 How can households get better predictability of premium hikes?
 For every health product, insurers could show how the premium has changed over the last five years. Ideally, the increase should be split between the impact of ageing and the insurer’s premium rate revision, which would largely reflect medical inflation, utilisation and claims experience. With greater product standardisation, changes in coverage should not distort this comparison.
 At the time of purchase, the insurer should also disclose the age-band structure clearly and indicate the maximum premium increase that could be imposed at one revision, apart from the disclosed impact of moving into a higher age band. That would give households a reasonable basis for planning.
 Do new products undermine risk pooling?
 Some insurers move claim-free customers into newer products, leaving those who have claimed in the old pool. As healthier customers leave, the remaining pool becomes more expensiv

Mint Money 
 Diwali fire hazards: how home insurance can protect your house and belongings
 Aprajita Sharma 7 min read 29 Oct 2026, 12:25 PM IST 
 Summary
 Diwali fire accidents can damage homes and belongings, leaving families with hefty bills. Here’s what home insurance covers, which add-ons to consider and how to avoid claim rejection. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Diwali is a festival of lights, but diyas, firecrackers and flowing garments can also increase the risk of fire accidents. While most households prioritize health and life insurance, home insurance often gets overlooked. Yet a fire can damage not just the structure of a house but also furniture, electronics, appliances, clothing and valuables, leaving families with a substantial financial burden.
 Home insurance can protect against such losses. It can cover damage caused by fire and smoke, lightning, storms, hail and other specified events. Add-on covers can provide protection against risks such as burglary, personal accidents, third-party liability and the cost of temporary accommodation if the house becomes uninhabitable.
 Homeowners must understand how home insurance works, how much cover they need and what the policy excludes.
 What does home insurance cover? 
 Home insurance typically has two components: the building and its contents. Homeowners can insure either or both, depending on their requirements. Building cover protects the structure, including walls, roofs, floors and permanent fixtures. Contents cover protects movable possessions such as furniture, electronics, appliances and clothing.
 "To calculate the insured value of the building, you need to consider the reconstruction cost per square foot and multiply it by the built-up area of the house. Insurers can help homeowners estimate the applicable construction cost," said Gaurav Arora, chief of commercial lines & motor (underwriting & claims) at ICICI Lombard .
 "For contents, homeowners should estimate the replacement cost or applicable insured value of their possessions and declare them under the relevant categories, such as electronics, appliances and clothing. The amount should reflect the value of the items being insured rather than an arbitrary figure," he added.
 Expensive possessions need particular attention. Jewellery , fine art, antiques, collectibles and high-end electronics may require an add-on and may have sub-limits.
 What happens if a fire breaks out? 
 Suppose a curtain catches fire on Diwali and the flames spread to the drawing room. The resulting damage to the building and insured contents will be covered under the fire section of the policy. Similarly, if a firecracker rocket enters the house or hits an air conditioner on the balcony and causes a fire, the resulting damage will be covered.
 What if a short circuit causes the fire? Electrical damage can be treated differently from fire damage. Ashwini Dubey, business head - home insurance, Policybazaar, shares an example.
 “If an air conditioner develops an electrical fault and catches fire, the policy may cover the resulting fire damage to the house and other insured belongings. However, the cost of repairing or replacing the faulty air conditioner itself may be excluded.”
 "Some policies or add-ons may offer broader protection against electrical or mechanical breakdown," he added.
 Is negligence covered? 
 Fire hazards can arise from the careless placement of diyas, candles or firecrackers during Diwali. Such carelessness or negligence in maintenance of the home, if found by a surveyor, can lead to claim rejection. Deliberate acts, wilful misconduct and specific exclusions will affect the claim for sure.
 "Avoid fireworks in enclosed spaces such as your balcony," suggested Dubey.
 "Homeowners should also follow basic precautions, such as keeping combustible materials away from diyas and not switching on electrical appliances in areas affected by flooding or fire until it is safe to do so," said Arora.
 What if a fire breaks out at a neighbour's property and spreads to your home? The damage to your insured property will be covered.
 "If the neighbour is found legally liable for causing the loss, third-party liability provisions and the principle of recovery may come into play," said Ramit Goyal, chief distribution officer, Generali Central Insurance. It means you do not have to wait for the neighbour's liability to be established before approaching your insurer. The insurer will admit your claim.
 Which add-ons are worth considering? 
 A personal accident add-on could help in case of accidental injuries or death. One can add self and family members under this add-on. A third-party liability add-on can cover legal liability if a visitor suffers bodily injury or their property is damaged at your premises and you are legally responsible.
 Consider a burglary add-on if you frequently travel or leave your house unoccupied. It covers the theft of insured contents.
 If a fire severely damages your home and makes it uninhabitable, an alternative accommodation benefit may reimburse eligible expenses for temporary accommodation.
 “We recently handled a case in which the insurer covered six months’ rent while the family stayed elsewhere during repairs to their home. Some insurers may provide this benefit for a longer period,” said Dubey.
 If you own a property that you rent out and fire or flood makes it unfit for occupation, a loss-of-rent benefit may compensate for eligible rental income lost during the covered period.
 Remember that temporary accommodation and loss-of-rent add-ons may have monetary or time limits. Read the add-on terms carefully before buying the policy.
 Mistakes to avoid while buying home insurance 
 If the house is registered in a parent's name but the child buys the policy, the insurer should be informed of the arrangement when the policy is issued.
 "Do not assume t

docs.title: Buy your next bike online. Here’s how to save more
docs.text:
Mint Money 
 Buy your next bike online. Here’s how to save more
 Shipra Singh 4 min read 29 Oct 2026, 03:04 PM IST 
 Summary
 Amazon and Flipkart offer two-wheeler buyers a way to stack platform discounts, bank offers and card rewards. But EMI costs, voucher limits and dealer fees can eat into the savings. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 When Bengaluru-based Anush Shenoy decided to buy a Harley-Davidson motorcycle recently, he placed the order on Amazon instead of visiting a showroom. The decision saved him ₹ 20,000 on a bike priced at ₹ 2.86 lakh, a discount of about 7%.
 Of this, ₹ 15,000 came from an Amazon coupon and another ₹ 5,000 from a credit card offer. “This doesn’t even include the indirect savings in the form of credit card rewards I’ve earned,” he said.
 Shenoy had already researched the motorcycle he wanted. On Amazon, he was asked to choose the dealership from which he would collect it. That choice mattered. "While selecting dealers I noticed the ₹ 15,000 coupon and credit card partnership discount was not available on all dealers. So I picked the one where I could maximize discounts," he said.
 He visited the selected dealer after booking, took a test ride and collected the motorcycle the same day. The dealer later said it could not match the online price. “In fact, he charged me a 1% service charge to use the same credit card to pay for RC (registration certificate), insurance and other smaller ancillary charges.”
 Shenoy’s experience shows how buying a two-wheeler through e-commerce platforms such as Amazon and Flipkart can cost less than purchasing it at a physical store. During the festive season, platforms offer higher discounts and credit card deals.
 On the same bike, Amazon is currently offering a ₹ 15,000 coupon, while the Amazon Pay ICICI credit card provides ₹ 13,300 cashback, taking the potential upfront savings to ₹ 28,300. This cashback is limited to Amazon Pay ICICI cards; other ICICI and Axis cards offer discounts of up to ₹ 11,000.
 How does it work? 
 E-commerce listings show the ex-showroom price, available dealers and applicable bank offers. Buyers select the model, variant and colour, enter their location and choose from the available dealers.
 They then pay the ex-showroom price online to book the bike. The dealer subsequently coordinates registration, insurance, KYC and document verification. Road tax, insurance, registration and other charges are payable separately.
 Buyers can collect the vehicle from the showroom after a test ride or opt for home delivery if the dealer offers it. Since these purchases are non-refundable, it is better to inspect and test-ride the vehicle before collecting it.
 How to maximize discounts and card rewards 
 The biggest advantage of buying online is the ability to combine platform coupons with instant discounts on credit cards issued by partner banks.
 Flipkart is currently offering upfront discounts of 9-11% on BGauss scooters, while Amazon is offering ₹ 2,500-10,000 off select Hero and Harley-Davidson motorcycles priced at ₹ 1 lakh or more. Offers vary by location, seller and payment method.
 Dealers generally do not offer comparable card discounts and may instead charge a processing fee of 0.5-3% for credit card payments. Buyers should compare the combined benefit available on cards they already hold. A ₹ 5,000 bank discount on one platform could make it cheaper than another with a larger coupon but no applicable card offer.
 Some of the biggest card discounts are available only on EMI transactions. Interest and processing charges can outweigh the upfront savings, so compare the total amount payable rather than the advertised discount alone.
 Earn through vouchers 
 Banks such as HDFC, ICICI and Axis offer additional rewards for buying Amazon Shopping Vouchers or Flipkart gift cards through their rewards portals. These can help maximise reward points on large purchases, said Akash Gupta, a credit card rewards and redemption consultant.
 “ Amazon shopping vouchers and Flipkart vouchers work on such purchases, which can be bought on multipliers using bank platforms. However, there are monthly caps, so it may not be possible to fund the entire purchase through vouchers, unless you plan in advance and buy vouchers every month for a couple of months,” he said.
 For instance, HDFC Bank’s SmartBuy offers 3X-5X reward points on vouchers for most premium credit cards, subject to a monthly accelerated rewards cap of 3,000 points.
 Consider a card that earns four points for every ₹ 200 spent and offers 3X rewards on Amazon vouchers bought through SmartBuy. It would earn 12 points per ₹ 200 on eligible voucher purchases. Paying directly for a ₹ 1 lakh bike would earn 2,000 points. Buying ₹ 30,000 in vouchers at 3X rewards and paying the remaining ₹ 70,000 directly by card would earn 3,200 points, or 1,200 additional points.
 Banks impose monthly limits on voucher purchases and accelerated rewards. Amazon and Flipkart also allow a maximum loading limit of ₹ 50,000 through vouchers.
 Buy vouchers up to the permitted limit and pay the balance by credit card to earn regular rewards or cashback. Before purchasing vouchers, confirm that they can be used to buy the vehicle and combined with bank discounts. These points represent indirect savings, whose value depends on how they are redeemed, not an upfront discount.
 Finally, check whether the dealership can match the final online price or offer better financing, insurance or accessories offline.
