docs.title: Hyundai jumps 6%: Brokerages see up to 31% upside but trim target price – Here’s why
docs.text: The Hyundai Motor India share price jumped nearly 6% in early trade on Thursday, October 29. The company’s revenue for the September quarter was higher than estimates. Several brokerages have maintained their ‘Buy’ ratings but lowered target price on account of margin pressure from high commodity inflation. Hyundai Motor Q2 earnings Hyundai Motor India’s consolidated net profit fell 23.9% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 1,196 crore in the September quarter, missing Bloomberg’s estimate of Rs 1,238 crore, as higher commodity costs eroded profitability despite strong growth in sales. Revenue rose 18.5% YoY to Rs 20,696 crore, beating the Bloomberg estimate of Rs 20,397 crore. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) declined 18.7% YoY to Rs 1,974.5 crore, below Bloomberg’s estimate of Rs 2,018 crore. EBITDA margin contracted to 9.5% from 13.9% a year earlier. ALSO READFrom packaging to defence: 3 stocks with FII stake hikes of up to 9.63 percentage points Motilal Oswal on Hyundai: Strong pipeline, export to drive volumes The brokerage reiterated its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock and has a target price of Rs 2,300. This implies an upside of 23% from the stock’s closing price of Rs 1,866.90 on Wednesday. Hyundai Motor is projected to deliver a 16% earnings growth on a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) basis over FY26 to FY28. Motilal Oswal believes the company remains well-positioned to benefit from the premiumisation trend in India, given its mix is skewed toward sports utility vehicles (SUVs). Hyundai’s net profit for the quarter was in line with Motilal’s expectations, despite commodity inflation adversely impacting margins. “The result was aided by higher volumes, favorable currency, price hikes, and cost-saving measures.” Motilal Oswal expects the company to post a 9% rise in volumes on a CAGR basis over FY26-FY28, driven by a strong pipeline and export order book. These include strong bookings for Bayon, another product launch in Q4, the ramp up of the third shift operations beginning at the Pune plant, and other product launches in FY28. “HMIL is targeting 8-10% domestic sales growth in 2HFY27 and FY27, supported by strong festive demand, resilient rural consumption, rising SUV traction, and new product launches. Exports are expected to record high double-digit growth in H2FY27, driven by new model introductions, market diversification, and alternative shipping routes, although geopolitical disruptions remain a key risk.” Nomura on Hyundai: Mass-market EV the key catalyst Nomura also retained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock and has a target price of Rs 2,442 apiece, implying an upside of nearly 31% from Wednesday’s closing price. The brokerage expects the new model cycle to drive potential market share gains in the second of the FY27 and in FY28. It expects the company’s domestic volume to grow at 11% in FY27, 13% in FY28, and 9% in FY29. Hyundai will maintain an export volume growth of 5% for FY27 due to the Middle-East conflict. “We believe exports can recover strongly in FY28F (+20% y-y), with more models and new markets. Strong growth should also drive margin expansion. A key catalyst will be the launch of mass market EV which could surprise positively,” Nomura said. The brokerage has trimmed EBITDA margin outlook to 10.6% for FY27 from 11.5%, and to 12.4% for FY28 from 12.7% earlier, due to higher cost pressures. “We believe the company has strong levers for margin expansion in 2H and beyond,” it added. Elara Capital on Hyundai: Better product mix, operating leverage The brokerage retained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock but cut the price target to Rs 2,400 due to persistent commodity pressures. This implies an upside of nearly 29% from the stock’s closing price on Wednesday. ALSO READEicher to TVS Motor: Why Jefferies is betting on two-wheelers this festive season “The success of the Bayon launch remains key on the back of which we factor in ~11-12% growth in FY28E, higher than the industry. We expect HMIL’s market share and margins to have bottomed out in H1 and expect an EBITDA growth of ~34 % YoY in H2FY27E on a low base. While commodity inflation remains a near -term concern, improving product mix and operating leverage should support earnings recovery,” the brokerage said. The company’s management reiterated its EBITDA margin guidance of 11% for FY27, implying margins at above 12% in the second half of the year. Incentives in Tamil Nadu and improving operating leverage providing visibility for margin recovery, Elara said. Hyundai Motor India: The way forward Despite missing estimates for net profit, Hyundai’s top line exceeded views. The company faces margin hurdles from rising commodity costs, but new launches and strong exports are expected to support future earnings. docs.title: Jefferies names 2 transformer stocks with up to 70% upside as AI data centres boost demand
docs.text: What if the biggest bottleneck in the world’s power supply is a giant metal box most people have never seen? Meet the transformer. Global investment bank Jefferies recently spoke to an industry expert about it, and the findings could matter for Indian stock investors. The global investment bank has assessed transformer demand in the United States and other global markets with the help of an industry expert. It remains positive on Siemens Energy India and Hitachi Energy India, citing domestic demand and potential export opportunities. But how much upside does it see, and what could drive these stocks? Siemens Energy vs Hitachi Energy: Jefferies price target and growth projection Jefferies has a ‘Buy’ rating on Siemens Energy India, with a target price of Rs 4,800, indicating an upside potential of 70%. Hitachi Energy India also has a ‘Buy’ rating, with a target price of Rs 45,790 and potential upside of 61%. The brokerage has a more cautious view on CG Power and Industrial Solutions, assigning it a ‘Hold’ rating with a target price of Rs 855 and upside potential of 2%. GE Vernova T&D India also has a ‘Hold’ rating, with a target price of Rs 4,850, implying an upside of 18%. ALSO READ2 ‘underdog’ stocks Mukul Agrawal and Vijay Kedia just added to their portfolios According to Jefferies, Siemens Energy India and Hitachi Energy India could see medium-term earnings per share (EPS) compound annual growth of more than 40%, supported by improved margins as higher business volumes spread operating costs across more sales. Why is transformer demand rising in the US? This is not limited to artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres. Ageing electricity grids in the United States also need replacement equipment, creating demand from utilities. Mayur Shah, from the sales and marketing team at Virginia Transformer Corp, told Jefferies that large transformers can last up to 60 years. The need to replace ageing equipment and upgrade grids is supporting demand, alongside new thermal power plants. According to the report, US transformer demand is growing at an annual rate of 4-6%, compared with largely flat growth in earlier years. Jefferies believes the impact may be temporary. Water requirements have held up some projects, but alternative cooling systems and more remote locations could help address these concerns. Rising AI usage and investment commitments by large US companies could continue to support electricity demand. Supply shortages give manufacturers pricing power Manufacturers are struggling with shortages of copper, bushings and other raw materials. These constraints are contributing to delivery delays and higher costs. However, buyers are absorbing increases in commodity and logistics costs, according to the industry expert cited in the report. Manufacturers are also charging higher fees for design changes. ALSO READ6 ‘Buy’ recommendations by Jefferies with 40% to 66% upside The lead times underline the supply-demand imbalance. According to Jefferies, Siemens Energy has delivery lead times of four to five years, while Hitachi Energy has lead times of three to four years. The industry is expanding capacity by 20-25%, but Jefferies expects demand to remain strong over the next five to seven years. Can Indian manufacturers win more export orders? The shift away from Chinese equipment could create an opening for alternative suppliers. Concerns about quality, after-sales service and electricity grid security are influencing purchasing decisions in the US. Jefferies highlighted CG Power’s transformer order from Tallgrass in the US for a data centre as an exception. It suggests that export logistics, rather than a lack of acceptance of Indian products, could partly explain the limited orders. The global investment bank also flags potential margin pressure for GE Vernova T&D India if exports account for a smaller share of revenue, and for CG Power if its industrial business faces weaker margins. docs.title: NSE: Jefferies initiates coverage, sees 17% upside as non-core units target Rs 2,242 cr
docs.text: Jefferies has initiated coverage on NSE with a ‘Buy’ rating and a price target of Rs 2,085, implying an upside of approximately 17.3%. The global investment bank believes the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) can benefit from this untapped demand, its leading position in exchange trading and opportunities to build revenue beyond its core business. Jefferies expects revenue to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 15% between FY27 and FY29, while earnings per share (EPS) are projected to rise at a 16% CAGR through FY29. Higher operating margins, technology services and new businesses could provide further support to earnings. NSE’s dominance provides a strong base for growth NSE held leading positions across cash equities, equity options, equity futures, and clearing and settlement. It accounted for approximately 93% of cash equity market share and 75% of equity options in FY26, while commanding virtually the entire equity futures market. Jefferies considers this market leadership a key advantage as trading activity expands and the exchange develops additional revenue streams. NSE generated revenue of Rs 16,600 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 17,100 crore in FY25. The brokerage expects revenue to increase to Rs 17,400 crore in FY27, Rs 19,800 crore in FY28 and Rs 23,000 crore in FY29. Stabilisation in equity options market share, higher cash market turnover and growing technology revenue are expected to support the recovery. Revenue growth is expected to accelerate through FY29 Jefferies expects NSE’s revenue to grow at a 15% CAGR over FY27-29, with EPS projected to increase at a 16% CAGR through FY29. The brokerage expects stronger revenue and operating leverage to support earnings growth over the period. NSE: Jefferies earnings estimates (FY27-FY29) Financial metricFY26 actualFY27 estimateFY28 estimateFY29 estimateRevenueRs 16,600 croreRs 17,400 croreRs 19,800 croreRs 23,000 croreAdjusted EBITDARs 12,700 croreRs 13,300 croreRs 15,300 croreRs 18,000 croreAdjusted EBITDA margin76%77%77%78%Adjusted EPSRs 43Rs 46Rs 53Rs 62 Source: Jefferies estimates. Figures are rounded. Adjusted EBITDA is projected to rise from Rs 12,700 crore in FY26 to Rs 18,000 crore in FY29. Adjusted EPS is expected to increase from Rs 43 to Rs 62 over the same period. Jefferies forecasts EBITDA margins to expand by around 200 basis points to 78% by FY29. Higher revenue and operating leverage are expected to support this improvement. Equity options regulation remains a key earnings risk Equity options accounted for around 60% of NSE’s operating revenue in FY26, making regulatory action in this segment important to its earnings outlook. Weekly index options represented approximately 40% of NSE’s revenue, compared with around 65% for BSE. Jefferies expects NSE’s equity options market share to stabilise at around 65%. The brokerage also noted that clients with low trading turnover accounted for around 2-3% of equity options premiums, limiting the potential impact of measures aimed at protecting small traders. The effects of earlier regulatory changes are expected to be largely absorbed in Jefferies’ forecasts. Stabilisation in options activity, together with growth in cash equities and other businesses, is expected to support revenue growth over the coming years. New businesses could generate Rs 2,242 crore by FY30 Commodity derivatives, electronic gold receipts (EGRs) and mutual fund order processing offer NSE opportunities to expand beyond its established exchange operations. Jefferies estimates that these businesses could generate combined revenue of Rs 2,242 crore by FY30. That amount would equal around 13.5% of FY26 revenue and 13.8% of FY26 profit after tax, according to the brokerage’s estimates. Their potential contribution is not included in Jefferies’ base-case forecasts. Commodity derivatives could benefit from new products and higher trading volumes, while NSE has scope to expand its presence in this segment. The brokerage estimates that EGRs could generate revenue of Rs 1,260 crore by FY30 as electronic receipts support the development of gold trading. Mutual fund order processing could add another source of revenue, with digital platforms providing opportunities to expand adoption. Jefferies sees these businesses as potential additions to earnings beyond its core forecasts. Technology services could grow at a 23% CAGR Data and technology services provide another source of potential growth for NSE. Jefferies estimates that these activities accounted for around 8% of FY26 revenue and expects them to grow at a 23% CAGR through FY29. NSE is also expected to add around 600 colocation racks over two years. These services could increase revenue from activities that are less directly tied to transaction volumes. Jefferies expects growth in technology services, alongside stronger core revenue, to support profitability. It forecasts EBITDA margins to reach 78% by FY29, compared with 76% in FY26. Low equity participation leaves room for expansion India’s direct equity investor base has increased around fourfold since Covid-19, according to Jefferies. However, direct equity participation remains at approximately 3% of the population, compared with 18% in China. The global investment bank expects further participation in financial markets to support trading activity and demand for exchange services over time. A broader investor base could benefit NSE as more individuals enter the equity market. Market volatility could also support revenue. Transaction charges on equity options are linked to premium turnover, so higher volatility can increase premiums and exchange revenue, while some operating costs do not rise proportionately. docs.title: Jefferies, JMFL see up to 52% upside in this flexible workspace stock under Rs 650
docs.text: WeWork India is expanding its flexible workspace network, but its next phase of growth will depend on how quickly newly added desks translate into higher occupancy and stronger earnings. The company has continued adding capacity while improving margins, and its growing contribution from value-added services is providing another source of revenue. Jefferies and JM Financial Institutional Securities (JMFL) see further earnings growth as new centres mature and operating efficiencies improve. Jefferies on WeWork India: ‘Buy’ “P&L beat, improving margins.” Jefferies used this phrase to describe WeWork India's September-quarter performance. The brokerage maintained its ‘Buy’ rating with a price target of Rs 950, implying 52% upside. Revenue rose 34% year on year and 12% sequentially to Rs 768 crore in the September quarter. Core rental revenue increased 32% year-on-year to Rs 660 crore, supported by a 33% increase in occupied desks. Adjusted EBITDA rose 42% year on year and 26% sequentially to Rs 160 crore, while the EBITDA margin expanded by 1.5 percentage points year on year to 21%. Jefferies said management expected further margin expansion as capacity additions made earlier in the year ramped up. EBITDA margins for FY28 were indicated at around 22% to 23%, depending on the pace and timing of capacity additions. The brokerage also described the company's capacity expansion as being absorbed well. Operational desk capacity increased by about 11,700 desks during the quarter, taking total capacity to 1,45,300 desks. Another 4,000 to 4,500 desks had been added in October, bringing capacity to the lower end of the company's target of 1,50,000 to 1,55,000 desks by March 2027. Portfolio occupancy improved by 3.6 percentage points year on year to 83.7%, while occupancy at mature centres reached about 88%. The sequential decline in overall occupancy reflected the ramp-up of newly added capacity. ALSO READNarayana Murthy’s family office buys 5th metal stock — The 68-year-old foundry monopoly Locked-in contract revenue rose 66% year on year to Rs 3,840 crore, significantly outpacing locked-in rental costs. This resulted in a locked-in revenue-to-rent ratio of 2.7 times. Jefferies raised its estimates and expected revenue and EBITDA to grow by 28% and 37%, respectively, in FY27. Between FY26 and FY29, it projected compound annual growth of 23% in revenue and 29% in EBITDA, supported by demand for flexible workspaces, premium pricing and operating leverage. The brokerage based its Rs 950 price target on 14 times estimated September 2028 enterprise value to EBITDA. Its upside case was Rs 1,100, while its downside case was Rs 600. Risks included a sharp downturn in office demand, slower desk additions and increased competition. ALSO READJSW Energy, Adani Energy, NTPC: Why Jefferies sees 39% to 54% upside in power utilities JMFL on WeWork India: ‘Buy’ “Margin-led earnings beat; trajectory remains upward.” JMFL used this description in its September-quarter report and retained its ‘Buy’ rating with a price target of Rs 850, implying 35.8% upside. The brokerage reported revenue of Rs 766.5 crore, up 33% year on year and 12% sequentially, exceeding its estimate by 4%. EBITDA increased 42% year on year and 26% quarter on quarter to Rs 160.7 crore, beating JMFL's estimate by 12%. The EBITDA margin expanded by 146 basis points year on year and 240 basis points sequentially to 21%. Core rental income stood at Rs 680 crore, up 34% year on year. Value-added services and digital products grew 27% and 46%, respectively, and together accounted for 14% of revenue, above JMFL's estimate of 12%. The company added about 11,700 desks during the quarter, with a substantial share of the new seats belonging to the managed segment. JMFL said the annual seat-addition target had largely been achieved and expected margins to improve towards the end of the financial year as the portfolio ramped up and rent-free periods expired. Operational capacity reached 1,45,300 seats, with overall occupancy at 83.7%. The mature portfolio comprised 1,20,300 seats and had occupancy of 87.7%, while growth centres, with around 25,000 seats, had occupancy of 65%. JMFL said WeWork India added 18,400 seats in the first half of FY27, followed by around 4,500 desks in October. With desk additions expected to moderate in the second half, the brokerage anticipated further margin improvement, particularly towards the fourth quarter. The brokerage raised its FY27 and FY28 IGAAP EBITDA estimates by 3% to 5% following the strong first-half performance. It expects revenue and EBITDA to compound at 22% and 27%, respectively, between FY26 and FY29, supported by additional seats and annual average revenue per member growth of 5%. JMFL also highlighted improving cash generation. Operating cash flow reached Rs 230 crore in the September quarter, up 143% year on year, while free cash flow turned positive at Rs 61.9 crore. The company moved to a net cash position of Rs 23.1 crore at the end of the quarter, compared with net debt of Rs 31.6 crore in the preceding quarter. JMFL retained its Rs 850 target while reducing the valuation multiple applied to estimated September 2028 enterprise value to EBITDA to 13 times from 15 times. docs.title: JSW Energy, Adani Energy, NTPC: Why Jefferies sees 39% to 54% upside in power utilities
docs.text: India’s power demand is running ahead of expectations, while renewable generation and merchant electricity prices are also rising. Jefferies raised its FY27 power demand growth forecast and named JSW Energy and Adani Energy Solutions Ltd. among its preferred private-sector utility stocks. It also favoured NTPC, citing the potential for earnings growth from stronger execution. The stock calls come as electricity demand strengthens across the sector, creating opportunities for companies expanding capacity and improving project execution. Jefferies raises FY27 power demand growth forecast to 9% Jefferies raised its estimate for India’s FY27 power demand growth to 9%, from 7%, after year-to-date growth exceeded 10%. It projected 6% growth for FY28, with further upside possible if El Niño conditions develop in calendar year 2027. Power generation rose 24% year on year in October 2026 month to date, marking the strongest monthly trend in 15 years apart from the post-COVID recovery in 2021. Renewable generation increased 26% year on year in FY27 to date, led by 47% growth in solar generation. Renewables accounted for 20% of total generation, up from 17% a year earlier. Thermal generation grew 10% and accounted for 68% of the total, while thermal plant utilisation rose to 68% from 62%. Average prices rose 46% year on year and 12% quarter on quarter to Rs 5.7 per unit in July-September 2026. October month-to-date prices climbed 2.6 times year on year to Rs 7.1 per unit. Renewable project awards reached 8.3 GW in FY27 to date, compared with 7.7 GW in the corresponding period a year earlier. The brokerage cited a stronger-than-expected September quarter, improving capacity additions and the potential for better execution. September-quarter EBITDA was 10% above Jefferies’ estimate, supported by higher generation and better merchant sales. Operations at KSK, which accounts for 12% of capacity, normalised after disruptions in the June quarter. The report stated, “Sep-quarter EBITDA was 10% above our estimates on higher generation and some better merchant sales.” JSW Energy’s installed capacity rose 15% year on year to 15.1 GW at the end of September. During the quarter, it added 301 MW of solar capacity and 212 MW of hybrid projects, and acquired the 300 MW Maruti thermal plant. Management remained confident of adding 3 GW of renewable capacity in FY27, including 1.6 GW in the second half. Jefferies expected EBITDA to grow 41% year on year in the second half, supported by stable KSK operations and new capacity. The report stated, “We believe execution ramp-up could help with multiple re-rating for JSWE, given the guidance miss in FY26 and spillover to FY27E.” Jefferies projected JSW Energy’s installed capacity to reach 25 GW by FY30, compared with the company’s target of 30 GW. Its estimates included annual organic renewable additions of 2 GW to 3.5 GW between FY27 and FY30, supported by 10.3 GW of renewable projects under construction. The report said, “Management said it expects the growth momentum to continue for another 3-5 years, beyond 2030, supported by C&I and group-captive RE opportunities, thermal additions, and the Bhutan hydro project.” Jefferies estimated revenue and EBITDA compound annual growth rates of 11% and 17%, respectively, between FY26 and FY30, and annual earnings-per-share growth of 46%. It also noted that 96% of JSW Energy’s operational portfolio was covered by long-term power purchase agreements. Its upside case carried a target price of Rs 800, implying 71% upside, while its downside case of Rs 390 represented a potential decline of 17%. Risks included delays in land acquisition, right of way, evacuation infrastructure and equipment supply. Jefferies on NTPC: ‘Buy’ Jefferies set a target price of Rs 425 for NTPC, implying 39% upside. It favoured the company on expectations of earnings growth from stronger execution. Stronger demand supports the utility outlook Jefferies’ higher power demand forecast comes alongside stronger generation, rising merchant prices and increased renewable project awards. JSW Energy’s capacity expansion and execution plans are central to its stock case, while Adani Energy Solutions and NTPC also feature among its preferred utility stocks. docs.title: Meesho: Why Nomura flags 27% downside while Jefferies, Motilal see up to 25% upside
docs.text: E-commerce player Meesho’s net loss for the September quarter narrowed year-on-year (YoY), with management signaling robust demand amid the festive season. However, brokerage views on the company remain mixed, with some expecting an upside of 25% while others see a 27% downside. Global investment bank Jefferies and domestic brokerage house, Motilal Oswal retained their ‘Buy’ ratings on the stock while Japanese brokerage Nomura maintained its ‘Reduce’ call. The Meesho share price was 0.1% lower at Rs 227.57 apiece. Meesho Q2 results Meesho reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 132.4 crore for the September quarter, compared with a loss of Rs 411.3 crore in the year ago quarter. Its consolidated revenue from operations grew around 34% to Rs 4,131.5 crore for the quarter. Jefferies on Meesho: Growth over monetisation Global investment bank Jefferies retained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock and has a price target of Rs 285. This implies an upside of 25% from the current price of Rs 227.57 apiece. ALSO READFrom packaging to defence: 3 stocks with FII stake hikes of up to 9.63 percentage points Meesho’s management remains confident around demand, driven by all-time-high festive traffic and better-than expected festive sales. However, they are watchful of macro conditions due to pressures from higher input and fuel prices. The company is confident of net merchandise value (NMV) growing at 25% on a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) basis through FY31, with steady improvement in margins. “However, the focus remains unapologetically on growth, with absolute clarity on offering value rather than rushing monetisation,” Jefferies said. Artificial intelligence (AI) led improvements in discovery and feed relevance are driving better user conversion and transaction frequency. “As workflows mature, more efficient models & lower-cost compute should help reduce cost of AI work over time. Also accelerated transition towards agent-led software development, driving up engineering productivity.” Motilal Oswal on Meesho: Advertising is the margin lever Motilal Oswal also retained its ‘Buy’ call on Meesho, with a target price of Rs 265. This implies an upside of 16% from the current price. “We believe Meesho’s asset-light model with negative working capital and improving unit economics makes for a unique combination of a scaled platform business with a long runway for growth and potential margin inflection,” the brokerage said. The company’s management retained the medium term guidance of around 25% NMV growth on a CAGR basis over FY26-FY31. Motilal said advertising remains the medium-term margin lever, with healthy seller demand for ads. “Higher ad monetization should drive CM expansion from FY28. FY27 CM should remain well above FY26, with logistics spread recovering to FY25 levels,” it added. Nomura on Meesho: 27% downside seen The Japanese brokerage maintained its ‘Reduce’ rating on the stock. Nomura has a target price of Rs 167 on Meesho, implying a downside of 27% from the current levels. The 140 basis point sequential improvement in contribution margin was a “positive surprise,” Nomura said. The primary driver of this growth was logistics efficiencies, including better return to origin (RTO) rates, increased order density, network redesign, and Valmo efficiencies. Brokerages reaffirm ‘Buy’ with up to 38% upside “Meesho’s management noted that the CM improvement will partly reverse in 3QFY27E due to the upcoming festive season as it plans to reinvest some near-term gains back into the business to fund growth and scale products and categories,” Nomura added. Meesho’s management said while its NMV growth is tracking slightly ahead of the guidance, it is too early to revise the same. “While Meesho management believes, it caters to the real value requirement of its customers, macro uncertainties particularly around supply challenges for its sellers due to volatile crude and crude derivative prices in the near term remains a key monitorable for them.” Meesho: The way forward The company is witnessing firm demand from the ongoing festive season in the country, with its management focused on growth over monetisation. However, supply chain worries remain due to volatile crude oil prices and other macro uncertainties, which remain a key factor to watch. docs.title: TVS Motor share price: Brokerages see 28% upside, but can PLI scheme’s end slow EV growth?
docs.text: Global and domestic brokerages remain bullish on leading two-wheeler maker TVS Motor Company, after it posted its quarterly results. Firm demand momentum for two-wheelers, strong volume growth outlook, and a healthy launch pipeline are expected to support the company’s performance in the coming quarters. Global investment bank Jefferies, Japanese brokerage Nomura, and domestic brokerage Motilal Oswal maintained their ‘Buy’ ratings on the stock, projecting up to 28% upside. TVS Motor Q2 earnings TVS Motor posted its highest ever revenue growth in Q2FY27, up 44% to Rs 17,103 crore from Rs 11,905 crore revenue growth recorded in the same quarter last fiscal. The company’s profit after tax jumped 52% to Rs 1,377 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 904 crore in Q2FY26. ALSO READFrom packaging to defence: 3 stocks with FII stake hikes of up to 9.63 percentage points The company reported its highest-ever quarterly earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) at Rs 2,219 crore, marking a 47% increase from Rs 1,507 crore in the year-ago period. Jefferies on TVS Motor: Two-wheeler demand firm in India, export markets The global investment bank retained its ‘Buy’ call on the stock, and has a target price of Rs 5,425 apiece. This implies an upside of 28% from the stock’s current price of Rs 4,222.70. Demand momentum for two-wheelers remains strong in both India and export markets and Jefferies prefers TVS' improving franchise and strong margin delivery amid rising commodity costs. Jefferies expects the company’s total volumes to grow 19% in FY27 and at 11% on a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) basis over FY27 to FY29. “Despite high base, registrations rose 16% in first 14 days of festive (11-Oct to 24-Oct). We assume 2W industry to grow 10% in FY27 and at 8% CAGR over FY27-29. TVS's exports remain strong, too, up 35% YoY in 2Q,” it said. TVS Motor expects pressures from high commodity costs to persist, albeit at a lower intensity than in the first half of FY27. Jefferies projects EBITDA margin of 13.3-14.2% over the second half of FY27 to FY29. The company has already taken some price hikes in Q3, although rupee has also slightly strengthened of late, which could pose some drag on export profitability, it added. Motilal Oswal on TVS Motor: Above industry growth in 2-wheelers The domestic brokerage retained its ‘Buy’ rating on TVS Motor and has a target price of Rs 5,200, implying an upside of 23% from the current price. Motilal Oswal has raised its earnings estimates for FY27 and FY28 by 11% and 10%, respectively, mainly due to strong margins in the September quarter, higher-than-expected realisations, and strong growth outlook in both domestic and export markets. “We expect this outperformance to continue, given its healthy new launch pipeline, which in turn is likely to help sustain its premium valuations,” the brokerage said. TVS Motor is expected to sustain above-industry level growth in domestic two-wheelers. This will be supported by market share gains, premiumisation, and “scooterisation”, despite industry growth moderating to single digits in the second half of FY27. Export volumes will be supported by improving product availability, new market entries, product launches, dealer-network expansion, and increasing penetration of electric two- and three-wheelers. Nomura on TVS Motor: EV demand to drive sales, market share Japanese brokerage Nomura has also maintained its ‘Buy’ call on TVS Motor and raised the target price slightly to Rs 4,605. This implies an upside of 9% from the current price. ALSO READEicher to TVS Motor: Why Jefferies is betting on two-wheelers this festive season Nomura expects strong growth momentum across segments, led by robust EV demand and exports. These should drive revenue growth and improvement in market share. The brokerage has raised its revenue growth outlook for TVS by 6% across FY27 to FY29, led by higher average selling prices. Nomura highlighted lower EV margins than ICE after the PLI scheme will end in FY28 as a key risk to its outlook. Other risks include large investments and capital expenditure straining free cash flows if growth is not commensurate. TVS Motor: The way forward Most brokerages remain positive on TVS Motor, highlighting growing demand in both domestic and export markets as key growth drivers. The company is also expected to sustain above-industry level growth in domestic two-wheelers. Pressure from high commodity costs are likely to persist, albeit at a lower intensity. However, the PLI scheme ending in FY28 is seen as a key risk to the outlook. docs.title: 2 ‘underdog’ stocks Mukul Agrawal and Vijay Kedia just added to their portfolios
docs.text: Mukul Agrawal and Vijay Kedia portfolio: 2 new stocks in the September 2026 filings The September 2026 shareholding filings have thrown up two names few investors knew a quarter ago. Both are small. Both trade on NSE Emerge, the exchange's platform for small and medium enterprises (SMEs). And both now carry the name of a market veteran on their register. Mukul Agrawal, who runs Param Capital, has taken a position in a Hyderabad maker of metal powders and tungsten parts that end up in rockets. Vijay Kedia, known for his SMILE approach to small companies, shows up in a Gujarat maker of technical yarns that listed only in September. The more telling detail is not what they bought. It is the price each paid to get in. One word of caution before the numbers. SME stocks follow lighter disclosure rules, trade in fixed lots rather than single shares, and can be hard to exit when buyers dry up. Read every figure below with that in mind. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now #1 Innomet Advanced Materials: Mukul Agrawal's Rs 25 crore tungsten defence bet Incorporated in 1984, Innomet Advanced Materials moved from diamond tools into metal powders in 2004 and now runs two divisions. One makes copper, bronze and nickel powders for auto parts and welding. The other, called Innotung, makes tungsten heavy alloys, an extremely dense metal used in defence, aerospace and radiation shielding. On its June 2026 earnings call, filed with NSE, the management said the company is qualified to supply pre-fragments for Pinaka rockets. It counts HAL and BDL among its tungsten customers. It also said China's curbs on tungsten exports have pushed buyers to look at India as an alternative. That is the hook for defence stock watchers. As per the September 2026 shareholding filing, Mukul Agrawal holds 2,26,200 shares, or about 1.7% of the company, worth roughly Rs 6.2 cr at today's price. The bigger move came next. On 23rd October 2026, the company informed NSE that it had allotted 11,92,200 warrants to him at Rs 210 each, a commitment of about Rs 25 cr. Each warrant can be converted into one share. Here is the twist. On 18th August 2026, Innomet had issued 4.5 lakh shares to non-promoter investors and 5 lakh warrants to its promoters, all at Rs 131. Mukul Agrawal's warrants are priced 60% higher. That gap reflects timing more than generosity, because SEBI's pricing rules tie such issues to recent trading prices, and the stock ran hard in between. If every warrant is converted, his holding would rise to roughly 9.4% of the enlarged share base. ALSO READ7x earnings, a 59% fall: Vijay Kedia and Dolly Khanna’s latest smallcap bets Innomet financials: 34% sales CAGR, but the profit line tells another story Financial YearFY21FY22FY23FY24FY25FY265Y CAGRSales (Rs cr)12.3022.1823.2924.9032.5253.8134%EBITDA (Rs cr)1.121.695.734.365.055.6038%Net Profit (Rs cr)0.200.553.222.521.871.57NM Source: Screener.in EBITDA here refers to operating profit before other income. NM: not meaningful, as the FY21 base is near zero. Sales have more than quadrupled in five years, and FY26 revenue alone jumped 66%. Profit is a different matter. Its five-year growth rate only looks dazzling because it starts from Rs 0.20 cr. Over three years, net profit has in fact shrunk by about 21% a year, from Rs 3.22 cr in FY23 to Rs 1.57 cr in FY26. Other income of Rs 0.32 cr also made up about 13% of FY26 pre-tax profit. The second half of FY26 was the weak spot. Sales rose to Rs 30.33 cr, yet the operating margin fell to 4.5% and the company posted a small loss of Rs 0.44 cr. The management blamed a sudden spike in tungsten and copper prices. It also wrote off Rs 1.92 cr of development costs the auditor could not validate, and reversed Rs 2.96 cr of revenue booked for a technology deal that fell through. Order book, Israel exports and the Swastik Tungsten buy The bull case rests on what comes next. Orders worth Rs 35.99 cr were booked in the first two months of FY27, the management said. That is more than half of last year's revenue, and about 77% of it is tungsten heavy alloys. A single export order from Israel's Scope Metals was pegged at about Rs 15 cr. In February 2026, Innomet also bought 57.5% of Swastik Tungsten through the NCLT route for around Rs 1.5 cr, to secure raw material. On 13th October, it disclosed fresh orders from Federal-Mogul Goetze and a Japanese buyer. Innomet share price and PE ratio: Priced at 228x earnings Innomet came to market in September 2024 at Rs 100 a share and listed at Rs 190. The share price of Innomet then slid to a 52-week low of Rs 63.2. A sharp rally took it to Rs 276 as of closing on 27th October 2026, more than four times that low. Shareholders have grown from 799 in September 2024 to 1,255. As for valuation, the stock trades at a PE of about 228x against a current industry median of about 20x. A 10-year median PE does not exist yet, as the stock has been listed for just over two years. At over eight times book value, with return on equity of 3.7% and return on capital of 5.7%, the price is a bet on the order book, not the past. Promoter holding slipped to 55.02% in September 2026 from 56.72% in March, largely because new shares went to other investors. More dilution lies ahead as warrants convert. ALSO READMukul Agrawal’s latest moves: A Rs 189 cr mining bet and 4 newly listed SME stocks #2 Ashutosh Fibre: Vijay Kedia's pre-IPO stake in a technical textile stock Incorporated in 1985, Ashutosh Fibre makes technical and synthetic yarns at a single plant in Petlad, Gujarat. These are not yarns for shirts. They go into filters, flame-retardant workwear, PPE kits, car seat fabric and carpets. Its IPO document, filed with NSE, shows exports made up about 39% of FY26 revenue, with China its largest export market. Kedia did not buy this one on the open market. He was already a shareholder before the IPO, with 6.57%

docs.title: Bajaj Auto vs TVS Motor: 1 hits 20.9% margin, 1 clocks 52% profit; Which stock stands out?
docs.text: The two-wheeler manufacturers have seen a strong Q2 despite cost pressures. Bajaj Auto and TVS Motor Company delivered robust performances in the September quarter of FY27. Bajaj Auto reported record quarterly revenue and profits, and TVS Motor grew revenue by 44% while increasing profit after tax by 52%. The difference lies in what happened beneath the sales numbers: TVS Motor improved its operating margin while Bajaj maintained a strong standalone margin. The companies’ earnings calls and results statements offer a closer look at how management plans to sustain momentum. Bajaj Auto spoke about records across its business and the need to recover rising costs. TVS credited its product range, pricing actions and cost-control measures for its performance. Their next challenge is to sustain demand without allowing higher costs to erode earnings. Bajaj Auto vs TVS Motor: Q2 perforamnce analysis Bajaj Auto’s September-quarter performance was marked by growth across revenue and profit. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 59.7% year on year to Rs 25,125.6 crore, while profit attributable to owners increased 61.9% to Rs 3,436.1 crore. On a standalone basis, revenue reached Rs 20,003 crore, and EBITDA stood at Rs 4,172 crore, giving the company an EBITDA margin of 20.9%, compared with 20.5% a year earlier. TVS Motor, meanwhile, reported revenue of Rs 17,103 crore, EBITDA of Rs 2,219 crore and profit after tax of Rs 1,377 crore. Revenue grew 43.7%, rounded to 44%; EBITDA increased 47% and profit after tax rose 52%, with the EBITDA margin improving to 13.0% from 12.7%. Bajaj delivered strong growth and a high standalone margin; Hyundai’s record sales came with a substantial decline in profitability, and TVS combined rapid revenue growth with an improvement in its margin. Each company now has a different task: managing costs at Bajaj, restoring margins at Hyundai, and sustaining growth at TVS. ALSO READNarayana Murthy’s family office buys 5th metal stock — The 68-year-old foundry monopoly Q2 FY27 metricBajaj AutoTVS MotorRevenueRs 25,125.6 crore consolidatedRs 17,103 croreRevenue growth59.7% consolidated43.7%EBITDARs 4,172 crore standaloneRs 2,219 croreEBITDA growth36.6% standalone47%EBITDA margin20.9% standalone13.0%Profit after taxRs 3,436.1 crore consolidatedRs 1,377 crorePAT growth61.9% consolidated52% Source: Company financials Bajaj Auto vs TVS Motor Company: What management said about the results Bajaj Auto’s earnings call on October 27, 2026, carried a celebratory tone, with Joint Managing Director Rakesh Sharma describing the quarter as “a festival of records in Q2.” The comment referred to the company’s performance across volumes, revenue, EBITDA, profit after tax and free cash flow. Chief Financial Officer Dinesh Thapar also spoke about the scale of the quarter, with volumes exceeding 15 lakh units, revenue crossing Rs 20,000 crore and EBITDA exceeding Rs 4,000 crore. The record performance came against a backdrop of higher input costs. Management discussed calibrated price increases to recover part of the inflationary impact, while acknowledging that cost pressures and currency movements remained relevant. The company’s challenge is to maintain its sales momentum while protecting margins in a market where price increases must be balanced against demand and competition. ALSO READJefferies, JMFL see up to 52% upside in this flexible workspace stock under Rs 650 TVS Motor’s results announcement on October 28 focused on its record sales and earnings. Chief Executive Officer K. N. Radhakrishnan said, “We are delighted to share that during this quarter, we achieved the highest-ever sales volume, revenue, and profits.” The company’s sales rose to 1.9 million units from 1.5 million units a year earlier, while revenue and profit after tax grew faster than volumes. Radhakrishnan also discussed the company’s response to commodity inflation, saying, “While there were commodity price increases in Q1 and Q2, we were able to take up some prices. We were able to partially mitigate through cost reductions. Also, optimization initiatives on product mix.” His comments connect the sales performance with the company’s margin improvement. Higher volumes helped drive revenue, while pricing, cost reductions and product mix helped contain the effect of rising input costs. Bajaj Auto vs TVS Motor Company: Demand growing across different vehicle categories Bajaj Auto’s growth was spread across domestic and international markets and across its internal-combustion-engine and electric products. Its business spans motorcycles, three-wheelers and electric scooters, giving it exposure to several categories rather than relying on a single vehicle segment. Management also discussed capacity constraints in high-end motorcycles, exports and electric vehicles. These constraints make production and supply important considerations alongside demand, particularly if the company continues to record strong volumes. TVS Motor sold 1.9 million units, up 27% year on year. Motorcycle sales increased 28%, scooter sales rose 29%, and international business grew 35%. Electric two-wheeler volumes reached 186,186 units, compared with 80,009 units a year earlier. Growth across motorcycles, scooters and electric products gives TVS several sources of demand, although sustaining this pace will depend on market conditions, product availability and the company’s ability to manage costs as volumes rise. Bajaj Auto vs TVS Motor Company: Margins reveal the pressure beneath revenue growth Bajaj Auto’s standalone EBITDA margin increased to 20.9% from 20.5%, while standalone EBITDA rose 36.6% to Rs 4,172 crore. The margin performance indicates that the company maintained operating profitability as revenue and volumes expanded. Management’s comments on inflation and calibrated price increases nevertheless show that cost recovery remains an ongoing task. The extent to which Bajaj can continue passing on higher costs will depend on consumer demand

docs.title: A Rs 7 crore dream, a Rs 26,000 SIP: This Rajasthan govt employee’s 17-year wealth plan
docs.text: Rajiv Solanki spends his working days keeping accounts. As a Senior Divisional Accountant in Rajasthan's Public Works Department in Jaipur, his job is to make sure the numbers add up and nothing is left off the sheet. His own retirement sheet has a gap in it. It may be the largest number on the page. Rajiv is 43. He has invested through SIPs for ten years, has built about Rs 32 lakh, and wants Rs 7 crore by the time he retires at 60. He is also unusually open about his doubts. "Rs 7 crore is the target I have in mind, but I want to understand whether my current investment plan will be enough," he says. That question deserves a straight answer. Getting there means running his numbers properly, and then looking at the one item his answers never mention. Everyday Crorepatis, Financial Express Digital's series on salaried Indians building serious wealth, has mostly featured people who have already crossed a big number. Rajiv is still in the middle of the climb, and he wants to know whether the route he has picked actually reaches the top. Building a Rs 32 lakh corpus on a government salary Rajiv is the only child of a retired state government employee and a homemaker. He did his BCom in Jaipur, cleared a competitive exam at 23, and has been in government service for about 20 years. His salary began at around Rs 35,000 a month and is now about Rs 1.55 lakh. That is a rise of roughly four and a half times over two decades, the steady climb of a government pay scale rather than anything dramatic. "Salary has increased over the years, but family responsibilities have also increased," he says. Those responsibilities are real. His wife is a homemaker. His son is 14 and in Class 8. As an only child, he looks after his parents as well. He owns a flat in Jaipur and pays an EMI of about Rs 18,000 a month on it. Household spending, including that EMI, comes to about Rs 82,000. "After all expenses, around Rs 55,000 is left with me," he says. He started investing about ten years ago with a Rs 10,000 monthly SIP and has raised it by around 10% each year. It now stands at about Rs 26,000. "I feel this is easier than starting with a very big SIP in the beginning," he says. On that path, he has put in roughly Rs 19 lakh in total. It is now worth about Rs 32 lakh. ALSO READHe started with ‘very bad’ mutual funds, yet built Rs 1 crore corpus at 29 The 11.5% reality check: Mutual fund returns vs. expectations That works out to an annual return of about 11.5%. That is close to what the broad Indian market has delivered. The Nifty 50 Total Return Index returned around 11.4% a year over the past 20 years, according to figures cited by Business Today in May 2026. Rajiv's money, in other words, has earned roughly the market's return. Sudhir Dandotiya, who appeared earlier in this series, described his own returns as fairly average and built a fortune anyway. Rajiv's sit in the same honest middle. His plan, however, assumes something better. He expects 13% to 14% a year from here. The same Business Today analysis puts the long-run return of Indian equities since 1990 at about 13.2% a year. Rajiv is penciling in a return at or above the market's 35-year average, and above what his own portfolio has actually earned. The Rs 50 lakh gap in his SIP plan The calculation below assumes he keeps his existing Rs 32 lakh invested, continues his Rs 26,000 SIP, raises it by 10% every year for the next 17 years, and earns the same return in every one of those years. Annual returnEstimated corpus at 6011%About Rs 4.7 cr12%About Rs 5.2 cr13%About Rs 5.8 cr14%About Rs 6.5 cr Even at the top of his own range, he falls about Rs 50 lakh short. To reach Rs 7 crore on this plan, his portfolio would need to earn roughly 14.6% a year for 17 years without a break. The gap can be closed with contributions rather than hope. At a 12% return, starting from about Rs 41,500 a month today instead of Rs 26,000, and still stepping up by 10% a year, would get him to Rs 7 crore. That is an extra Rs 15,500 a month from the Rs 55,000 he has left. Before he finds that money, though, there is a more important question to settle. How the Old Pension Scheme could change his retirement math In its 2022 budget, Rajasthan became the first state to bring back the old pension scheme, for employees appointed on or after January 1, 2004. The current government has also continued the scheme. Rajiv joined state service about 20 years ago, which places him in that cohort. Under the old scheme, a retiring employee typically receives about half of the last drawn basic pay as a pension for life, with dearness relief revised twice a year to keep pace with prices. Not one of his answers mentions a pension. Whether he is covered, and on what terms, is something only his own service records can confirm. If he is covered, he is likely to retire on a handsome pension. He still has about 17 years of service left. Pay commissions come roughly once a decade; the 8th, constituted in November 2025, has yet to submit its report. Rajasthan has followed earlier central commissions with its own pay revisions. Rajiv is likely to benefit from at least two such revisions before he retires, and each would raise the base on which his pension is calculated. Putting a figure on it today would be guesswork, since the amount depends on pay commissions and dearness allowance increases that have not happened yet. But a lifelong income that rises with prices is exactly what most private-sector employees try to build through their investments. Naresh Bhardwaj, the first person profiled in this series, spent 17 years putting money into NPS so he could buy a pension of about Rs 1 lakh a month. Rajiv may already have a pension written into his terms of service. His father, a retired state government employee, belongs to the generation for whom that was simply assumed. docs.title: ONGC vs Oil India: Kotak sees 57% upside in one but 20% downside in another — Here’s why
docs.text: Crude prices continue to be at uncomfortably high levels and how is it impacting two major oil producers in India. Both are state-run. Both are upstream oil companies but Kotak Institutional Equities expects a sharp rise for one and flags concerns about the other one. Kotak Institutional Equities has maintained a ‘Buy’ rating on ONGC, with a fair value of Rs 360, implying a potential upside of 57% from the October 27 price of Rs 230. In contrast, it has retained a ‘Sell’ rating on Oil India, with a fair value of Rs 365, indicating a potential downside of 20% from Rs 457. According to the brokerage report, the difference comes down to production prospects, oil and gas realisations, and the ability to benefit from higher prices. Here is a detailed analysis of the brokerage’s investment rationale for the two upstream oil companies. ONGC vs Oil India: What is behind Kotak’s divergent calls? Kotak’s preference for ONGC rests on its medium-term production outlook and the scope for better gas realisations. According to the brokerage report, ONGC’s partnership with BP for its Western Offshore asset could support production. This asset accounts for around 70% of ONGC’s output. The brokerage also sees support from pricing for new-well gas (NWG), which could improve realisations, or the prices received for the gas sold. New fields are expected to contribute to production growth, although the company has faced setbacks at its KG-98/2 project. ALSO READFrom packaging to defence: 3 stocks with FII stake hikes of up to 9.63 percentage points Oil India, meanwhile, faces concerns over its longer-term oil production. Kotak believes its limited reserves could lead to a decline in oil output after a near-term increase. The company’s gas production outlook is relatively better, but weak oil and gas realisations and margins remain concerns. Crude oil at $100: Why has Kotak raised its estimate? The brokerage has raised its FY27 crude oil price assumption to $100 per barrel from $90 per barrel. It has retained its assumption of $75 per barrel for FY28 and the longer term. The revision comes amid continuing supply disruptions linked to the West Asia conflict. Although oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered significantly, renewed hostilities and attacks on energy infrastructure have kept supply risks in focus. According to Kotak, dated Brent crude averaged $126 per barrel in October up to the report date and $104 per barrel on a FY27 year-to-date basis. Higher oil prices could support earnings for both companies. The brokerage has increased its FY27 earnings estimates by 16-17% for ONGC and Oil India. This is driven by better crude oil and new-well gas realisations. However, it continues to prefer ONGC because of its stronger medium-term production prospects and valuation. Policy changes could offer another boost Changes in upstream oil and gas policies have also improved the operating environment, according to Kotak. Amendments to the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Act (ORDA), royalty reforms and the Samudra Manthan initiative are among the measures cited by the brokerage. These changes could allow producers to benefit more directly from higher oil prices. Kotak also considers the pricing mechanism for new-well gas, linked to 12% of Brent crude, favourable compared with earlier arrangements. ALSO READMeesho: Why Nomura flags 27% downside while Jefferies, Motilal see up to 25% upside ONGC or Oil India: What should investors watch? Kotak has raised ONGC’s fair value to Rs 360 from Rs 355 and Oil India’s to Rs 365 from Rs 360. Despite increasing both estimates, its ratings remain unchanged - ‘Buy’ for ONGC and ‘Sell’ for Oil India. Apart from the key difference of the direction of crude oil prices, it is how each company can convert favourable prices into sustainable production, better realisations and stronger earnings. For ONGC, the brokerage sees potential from its Western Offshore partnership and gas pricing. For Oil India, concerns about reserves, future oil output and margins weigh on its outlook. docs.title: NTPC to Tata Power: Bernstein sees up to 50% upside in 6 stocks amid data centre boom
docs.text: Every app you open, every video you stream, every AI chatbot you try runs on data centres. These are giant buildings full of computers. They eat enormous amounts of electricity. The key question now is - who is actually lining up for that power in India? Also, India’s data centre boom is creating a new question for investors - which companies could benefit from the massive electricity requirements of artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing? According to the Bernstein report, India’s data centre opportunity is becoming more visible through applications for electricity connectivity across central and state grids. Why is Bernstein tracking data centre power demand? A data centre is a facility that houses computer servers used to store information, run applications and support digital services. These facilities require a steady supply of electricity to operate servers and cooling systems. Securing grid connectivity is therefore a critical step before a project can become operational. ALSO READRs 1,000 cr AI deal, 334.8% profit growth: 2 stocks riding India’s GPU boom Bernstein’s report pointed to a sharp increase in India’s estimated electricity requirements. The Ministry of Power’s estimate of data centre power demand for 2032 doubled from around 14 gigawatts (GW) to approximately 26 GW between March and July, according to the brokerage’s account of a parliamentary filing. The report also mapped applications for around 35 GW of connectivity across central and state grids, of which 12 GW had received approval. The brokerage cautions that approvals do not guarantee completed projects. “How much finally materializes remains to be seen,” the report said, highlighting the scale of investment required and uncertainty over funding. However, Bernstein believes India could still meet the government’s initial demand projections. Bernstein’s top power and infrastructure stocks The brokerage’s recommendations cover companies involved in engineering, electricity generation and transmission. Stock targets: How much upside does Bernstein see? StockRatingTarget priceUpside potentialNTPCOverweightRs 45050.00%Tata PowerOverweightRs 43027.00%Power GridOverweightRs 31326.70%Larsen & ToubroOverweightRs 4,63726.00%Adani PowerOverweightRs 22017.90%NTPC Green EnergyMarket PerformRs 854.00% Which companies are leading the connectivity race? The central grid offers an early indication of which companies are preparing to build data centres. Bernstein identified around 4.4 GW of demand that could be directly linked to data centres based on applicant names. Another 6.5 GW could be inferred from the parent companies of applicants. ALSO READJefferies names 2 transformer stocks with up to 70% upside as AI data centres boost demand The Adani group stands out in this assessment. According to the brokerage report, it is the only applicant with around 1.5 GW of approved connectivity for data centre use, alongside another 6-8 GW of applications directly associated with such projects. Reliance Industries also has around 14 GW of demand under process. However, Bernstein expects this to cover several uses, including captive power, green hydrogen and data centres. It cautions against treating the entire amount as data centre demand. Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh emerge as key markets At the state level, Maharashtra remains an important data centre hub. The brokerage mapped around 8 GW of approved or pending connectivity, with Navi Mumbai accounting for a substantial share. Applicants include global technology companies and data centre operators, alongside real estate developers. Andhra Pradesh is also attracting investment. Bernstein mapped around 4 GW of data centre grid approvals, excluding the Google-Adani project tracked through the central grid. These include projects linked to Reliance, ReNew, Sify, Greenko and other operators. State incentives, including electricity tariff concessions and exemptions from certain charges, could support development. Tamil Nadu, traditionally another major data centre destination, could see fresh applications if its proposed policy encourages further investment. docs.title: GST relief for FPIs may benefit brokers and depositories, says Jefferies
docs.text: A government clarification exempting eligible brokerage services for overseas investors from goods and services tax (GST) could lower the cost of investing in Indian equities, potentially benefiting stockbrokers and depositories if it leads to higher cash-market turnover, according to Jefferies. The brokerage expected the earnings impact on stock exchanges to be comparatively lower. In a circular dated October 26, 2026, the Ministry of Finance clarified that brokerage paid by overseas clients, including foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), non-resident Indians (NRIs) and overseas citizens of India (OCIs), from repatriable Indian rupee accounts qualifies as an export of services and therefore does not attract GST. ALSO READ2 ‘underdog’ stocks Mukul Agrawal and Vijay Kedia just added to their portfolios Jefferies said the clarification could reduce investing costs amid discussions about tax cuts for investors. The brokerage identified a potential benefit for brokers and depositories if the lower tax burden led to an increase in cash-market turnover, while expecting a lower earnings impact for exchanges. ALSO READNSE: Jefferies initiates coverage, sees 17% upside as non-core units target Rs 2,242 cr Jefferies sees potential benefits for brokers and depositories Jefferies said higher cash-market turnover resulting from the tax relief could benefit stockbrokers and depositories, while stock exchanges could see a comparatively lower earnings impact. The brokerage stated in its report, “Tax break led cash turnover rise could be a positive for brokers/depositories, with lower earnings impact for exchanges.” The potential benefit depends on whether the GST clarification leads to higher cash-market turnover. GST clarification covers eligible overseas brokerage payments The Ministry of Finance circular clarified the GST treatment of brokerage paid by overseas clients from repatriable Indian rupee accounts. Under the clarification described by Jefferies, these payments qualify as exports of services and do not attract GST. The relief applies to eligible brokerage payments by FPIs, NRIs and OCIs, subject to the conditions set out in the circular. It should not be read as a blanket exemption covering every brokerage transaction. Jefferies noted that the clarification came amid discussions about tax cuts for investors, including a report published by The Indian Express on October 13, 2026. FPI equity outflows exceeded $50 billion across CY25 and CY26 year to date Jefferies' data showed substantial net FPI selling in Indian equities. Net equity outflows stood at $18.8 billion in calendar year 2025 (CY25) and $32.3 billion in calendar year 2026 to date (CY26TD). The report's chart also showed net FPI equity inflows of $21.4 billion in CY24. The combined outflows recorded in CY25 and CY26TD exceeded $50 billion. Jefferies did not suggest that the GST clarification would reverse the outflows. Its assessment focused on the potential effect of lower brokerage-related costs on cash-market turnover and the resulting implications for market intermediaries. Conclusion Jefferies' assessment was conditional on the tax relief leading to higher cash-market turnover. If that occurs, brokers and depositories could benefit, while the earnings impact on exchanges could be comparatively lower. docs.title: Jio Platforms races past brokerages’ 12-month targets on debut
docs.text: Jio Platforms has taken just one trading session to race past the 12-month price targets set by some of the leading brokerages. The stock's stellar market debut on Wednesday saw it close at Rs 1,419, up nearly 27% from its issue price of Rs 1,119 and comfortably above the targets set by Nomura, Motilal Oswal Financial Services and Elara Capital. All three brokerages initiated coverage with a 'Buy' rating, betting on higher average revenue per user (ARPU), tariff hikes, expansion in home broadband and new revenue streams from digital services and international technology licensing. ALSO READJio Platforms financials: Telecom arm draws 87% revenue; rising debt costs signal caution The sharp listing-day rally, however, has already taken the stock 3.8–5.9% above their 12-month price targets, raising questions about how much of Jio's growth potential is already reflected in its valuation. Nomura, which initiated coverage on Wednesday with a target price of Rs 1,340, had projected an upside of nearly 20% from the issue price. The brokerage expects Jio to leverage its high data consumption per subscriber and low customer churn to drive ARPU growth. An anticipated industry-wide tariff hike in November–December 2026 could provide an immediate earnings trigger. Nomura also identified home broadband expansion, international licensing opportunities for Jio's proprietary unlicensed band radio (UBR) technology and declining capital expenditure as key growth drivers. Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL), which set a target price of Rs 1,350, expects Jio to consolidate its leadership in wireless services. It projects a 100-basis-point increase in the company's revenue market share between FY26 and FY29, alongside Jio accounting for 73% of incremental industry subscriber additions in home broadband during the period. The brokerage also sees significant opportunities beyond traditional connectivity services. “Scaling up its digital platforms, including cloud, enterprise communications, internet of things (IoT), and managed services, along with international tie-ups for its 5G/UBR technology, will offer the next leg of growth beyond the connectivity business,” MOFSL said. ALSO READJio IPO listing: Buy, Hold or Avoid? Top market experts weigh in Elara Capital, which assigned the highest target price among the three at Rs 1,367, is particularly bullish on Jio's emerging digital services business. The brokerage believes Jio is leveraging its affordable data offerings and extensive telecom network to build a large-scale digital products and services ecosystem catering to consumers and enterprises. Elara expects digital services revenue to double by FY30, expanding at twice the pace of the telecom business and emerging as the company's biggest growth driver. Meanwhile, Jio's telecom subscriber base is projected to grow at 3% annually between FY26 and FY29, supported by affordable tariffs, extensive network coverage and low churn.

docs.title: Noida to develop AI city with GCCs, IT firms and start-ups
docs.text: The Noida Authority has given in-principle approval to a proposal to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) city-cum-business park through private sector participation. The move is seen as part of Uttar Pradesh's push to steps up efforts to attract multinational corporations and technology companies, reported The Indian Express. ALSO READVaranasi Ropeway: Second-phase trial run underway — Route, ticket price here The decision was taken at the authority's 224th board meeting on Wednesday, following the adoption of the Uttar Pradesh Private Business Park Development Scheme, 2025. The proposal includes inviting bids to select a master developer for the project. At least 50% of the park's built-up area will have to be reserved for IT and knowledge-based services, officials said. Uttar Pradesh cabinet recently approved the development of a robotics and artificial intelligence park in Greater Noida. AI city to house GCCs, IT firms and start-ups The proposed park will provide infrastructure for artificial intelligence, Global Capability Centres (GCCs), IT services, research, start-ups and skill development, according to officials. “The project will include facilities for AI, Global Capability Centres, IT services, research, start-ups and skill development. It will follow the Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) model,” the official said, adding that the ownership of the land will remain with the Noida Authority. The concession period for the project will be 45 years, with a provision to extend it by another 45 years. The developer will be selected through competitive e-bidding, official said, reported The Indian Express. Separately, the authority approved the publication of a land allotment plan for a Global Capability Centre hub and Grade-A office space in Sector 147. The development will cover around 68,000 square metres of institutional IT/ITES land. Noida to develop automobile complex, finalise logistics plan The authority also approved the development of an integrated automobile complex on 12,596.64 square metres of commercial land in Sector 105. In another decision, the board cleared the final report of the City Logistics Plan prepared for Noida. The plan examines industrial and commercial activities alongside traffic management to improve the movement and distribution of goods. ALSO READDilip Buildcon bags Rs 688 crore NHAI order to build 4-lane corridor in Maharashtra Officials said the initiative aims to make logistics operations more efficient, lower transportation costs and reduce traffic congestion. “It is decided to forward it to the state government for approval,” the official said.

 Shares of Tata Group retailer Trent Ltd. will be in focus on Friday, October 30, after the company reported its September quarter results, with operating performance ahead of analyst estimates, supported by margin expansion and growth in its Star business.
The company’s consolidated EBITDA stood at ₹1,078 crore, compared with the CNBC-TV18 poll estimate of ₹896 crore. The EBITDA margin came in at 18.4%, ahead of the estimated 15.7%.
Profit after tax (PAT), however, was marginally below expectations at ₹468 crore against the poll estimate of ₹475 crore.
Trent had reported revenue growth of 22% in its Q2 business update. Its like-for-like growth in the fashion portfolio was in the mid-single digits during the quarter.
Emerging categories, including beauty and personal care, innerwear and footwear, contributed 21% to revenue. Its Star business reported revenue growth of over 20% during the quarter.
The company said consumer sentiment remained broadly positive, although inflation across various cost categories continued to remain elevated.
Jefferies has maintained its 'Hold' rating on Trent, with a price target of ₹3,300. The brokerage said that while revenue growth was already known from the company's pre-quarter business update, margin expansion drove a 37% year-on-year increase in pre-Ind AS EBITDA. However, the metric came in below its estimates.
Fashion LFL growth improved to the mid-single digits during the quarter, despite a shift in festive seasonality, Jefferies said.
The brokerage expects the results to support investor sentiment and could lead to a positive near-term reaction in the stock. However, it cautioned that higher input costs could weigh on margins in the near term and potentially affect demand.
HSBC has retained its 'Buy' rating on Trent and a price target of ₹3,480. The brokerage said the company's Q2 EBITDA was around 2% ahead of its estimates, supported by gross margins holding up better than expected despite anticipated raw material cost pressures.
LFL growth in the fashion business also improved to the mid-single digits, compared with low-single-digit growth in Q1 FY27, despite the shift in festive seasonality.
HSBC has raised its FY28 EBITDA estimate by 2%, while marginally lowering its earnings per share estimate due to changes in its assumptions on other income.
Citi has maintained its 'Sell' rating on Trent, with a target price of ₹2,815. The brokerage said revenue and EBITDA grew 23% and 30%, respectively, year-on-year, coming in 4% and 1% above its estimates. However, a 71% year-on-year decline in other income meant that profit after tax grew by 9%, 3% below its estimate.
Citi identified gross margin expansion as a key positive surprise. Gross margins improved by 121 basis points year-on-year despite raw material inflation.
The brokerage also said that pre-Ind AS rent and operating expenses per square foot declined 8% and 11%, respectively, while employee costs per square foot increased 5%. Fashion LFL growth was in the mid-single digits, although revenue per square foot declined 8.4% year-on-year.
Citi said the sustainability of margins amid raw material and operating cost inflation in the second half of the financial year would be a key factor determining the stock's performance.
While the brokerage continues to like Trent's business model and execution track record, it said it would wait for more attractive valuations and/or a successful scale-up of newer pilot formats before adding exposure to the stock.
Nuvama Institutional Equities has maintained its 'Buy' rating on Trent but lowered its price target to ₹3,466 from ₹3,591 earlier.
The brokerage said Trent reported standalone revenue, operating EBITDA and adjusted PAT growth of 23%, 38% and 9%, respectively, year-on-year, supported by mid-single-digit like-for-like growth.
Operating EBITDA margin expanded by 150 basis points, aided by a 121-basis-point improvement in gross margin and operating leverage on other expenses.
Nuvama noted that management had flagged supply chain disruptions but was addressing them through wider engagement with suppliers. The brokerage also highlighted a pick-up in growth at Star, which reported a 20% year-on-year increase in revenue after five quarters of slower growth.
The brokerage has revised its revenue and EBITDA estimates for FY27 and FY28. It raised its FY27 revenue and EBITDA estimates by 1.4% and 1.9%, respectively, while revising its FY28 estimates by 0.3% and -0.3%, respectively.
Nuvama said Trent was trading at 70 times and 57 times its estimated FY27 and FY28 earnings per share, respectively.
Separately, Trent’s board has approved the appointment of Bahram Vakil as chairman, following Noel N. Tata’s retirement from the position with effect from November 11, 2026.
Trent shares ended 1.79% lower at ₹2,861.70 on Thursday. The stock has remained broadly flat so far in 2026.

docs.text:
Published On Oct 30, 2026 | 07:22 IST 
 Last Updated On Oct 30, 2026 | 07:49 IST

 Copy Link 
 Summary
 Investec, ICICI Securities, and UBS all have "buy" ratings on Suzlon Energy, with price targets of ₹56, ₹55 and ₹58 respectively. None of the 11 analysts tracking the company have a "sell" rating on the stock.
 + Follow on Google Add as preferred source 
 Shares of Suzlon Energy Ltd. will be in focus on Friday, October 30, as the stock will react to its September quarter results, that were reported after market hours on Thursday.
During its earnings call, Suzlon Energy's management revised the full year EBITDA margin guidance down to 15% plus-minus, from the earlier guidance of 17% plus-minus. 
For the second quarter, the Wind Turbine Generator (WTG) contribution margins declined to 21.2% from 26.9% last year due to non-recurring opex (100 bps), consumer / scope mix (150-180 bps), and 50 bps from forex and commodity volatility.
The management expects the WTG contribution margin to now be between 22% to 23% for the full financial year, expecting normalization as external factors resolve.
India's market is projected to reach 15 GW by financial year 2035 and Suzlon is confident of achieving 40% market share target by that period.
For the September quarter, Suzlon Energy's net profit appears to have declined by 69% from last year, but that appears so due to an exceptional gain in the base quarter, which resulted in the profit back then to be elevated.
Revenue for the quarter increased by 26% from last year. Operating performance turned out to be weak, with Earnings before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) for the quarter remained flat at ₹713 crore, while margins narrowed to 14.7% from 18.7% last year. 
 Brokerage firm Nuvama said that it has cut its financial year 2027 and 2028 Earnings Per Share (EPS) estimates by 9% and 7% respectively, and is also introducing estimates for financial year 2029 to account for the EPC-led increase in costs.
The brokerage has maintained its "hold" rating on Suzlon but has slashed its price target to ₹41 from ₹51 earlier. 
 Nuvama went on to write that while Suzlon's financial year 2031 targets are encouraging, the growth is likely to be back-ended and dependent on the success of DevCo, where it is a late entrant.
Investec maintained its "buy" rating on Suzlon Energy with a price target of ₹56, stating that they are expecting annual order intake of 3.5 GW - 3.6 GW and retain their execution estimates for this and the next financial year.
The brokerage expects Suzlon Energy's revenue to grow at a compounded annual growth rate of 27% and a PBT CAGR of 21% over financial year 2026-2028. Its net cash position, strong RoE and RoCE, along with attractive valuations keep them bullish on the stock.
ICICI Securities has also cut its price target on Suzlon Energy to ₹55 from ₹65 earlier but maintained its "buy" recommendation on the stock citing favourable valuations.
It wrote in its note that the company is laying the ground work for its next leg of growth, adding that the wind turbine deliveries are pacing well and commissioning is also now catching up with deliveries.
"Suzlon's margins take a hit partly due to commodity and forex inflation and higher expenses on spend towards Suzlon 2.0. Though the impact is likely to be a passing cloud, the near-term numbers are expected to be impacted," ICICI Securities wrote in its note.
Despite the subdued results, majority of the analysts tracking Suzlon continue to have a "buy" recommendation on it. 10 out of the 11 analysts covering the stock have a "buy" rating on it, while one has a "hold" rating. None of the analysts have a "sell" rating on the stock. The consensus estimates of price targets implies an upside potential of 56.1% from current levels.
Investec, ICICI Securities, and UBS have "buy" ratings on Suzlon Energy, with price targets of ₹56, ₹55 and ₹58 respectively.
Shares of Suzlon Energy ended 1.4% lower on Thursday ahead of the results announcement at ₹36.79. The stock is down 30% on a year-to-date basis.

 Tanushree Singh Updated Oct 29, 2026 3:15 PM IST
 Gravita India shares touched a high of Rs 1,400.75, up 4.26% from the previous close of Rs 1,343.50. 
 Axis Securities maintained its BUY recommendation on Gravita India with a target price of Rs 2,270 per share, while Emkay Global retained its BUY rating with a target price of Rs 2,100.
Gravita's net profit stood at Rs 102 crore in Q2 FY27, up 6% from Rs 96 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Adjusted Ebitda was largely in line with the estimate in Axis Securities' result update, while revenue exceeded its estimate by 5%. The adjusted Ebitda margin was 10%, compared with 10.75% a year earlier, although it improved 25 basis points sequentially.
Gravita India shares touched a high of Rs 1,400.75, up 4.26% from the previous close of Rs 1,343.50. The stock opened at Rs 1,350.05 and touched a low of Rs 1,317.20 during the session.
 Copper business supports quarterly performance 
The company's copper business contributed Rs 420 crore to Q2 FY27 revenue following the integration of Rashtriya Metal Industries Ltd (RMIL). Copper Ebitda per metric tonne increased to Rs 84,671 from Rs 55,151 in the previous quarter, according to Axis Securities' report. RMIL recorded an Ebitda margin of 8.5% during the quarter, as cited in the report's conference-call highlights.
 Lead volumes affected by supply disruptions 
Lead recycling volumes declined 11.3% YoY to 39,203 metric tonnes from 44,187 metric tonnes in Q2 FY26. The research reports attributed the decline to raw-material shortages and supply-chain disruptions linked to West Asia and Red Sea transit delays, rather than weaker end-user demand. Management expects lead volumes to improve from Q3 FY27 as sourcing diversification and domestic procurement increase.
 Gravita outlines capacity expansion plans 
Gravita has earmarked Rs 1,680 crore in capital expenditure through FY29, including Rs 815 crore for existing businesses and Rs 865 crore for new verticals such as copper and lithium-ion battery recycling. Its installed recycling capacity is targeted to increase from around 480,000 metric tonnes per annum to more than 800,000 MTPA by FY29. The company is also developing a 29,400-MTPA copper recycling facility at Mandvi, Gujarat, and plans to add 59,200 MTPA of copper recycling capacity at Mundra in phases by March 2029.
